filing_statement:
WHAT CANON REQUIRES. JPWB-DOC-003 §5 STA-4, limb 1 (canon L187), verbatim: "Proposed work cannot execute;". The invariant is enforceable on TWO planes and this repository enforces exactly one of them.

THE PLANE THAT HOLDS (stated first, because it is why the gap is invisible). packages/rph-domain/src/transitions.data.ts:608-612 declares PWU.workLifecycleState PROPOSED -> EXECUTING ILLEGAL, reason "§8.3 — must be rejected; skips SHAPING→READY→PLANNED gating." A ChangePwuState asking the PWU to SAY it is executing is refused RPH_ILLEGAL_STATE_TRANSITION. So limb 1 holds against the DECLARATION and fails against the ACT.

WHAT THE CODE DOES. packages/rph-domain/src/execution.ts:148 `canResumeExecutionOnPwu(pwuLifecycleState)` answers "is this PWU CLOSED?", not "is this PWU OPEN?". It refuses the BASELINED literal (RPH_BASELINED_PWU_NO_RESUME, :149-155) and — since JAN-EXECREM WP-12b / F-28 — the machine's own derived terminal set {BASELINED, ABANDONED, SUPERSEDED} (RPH_CLOSED_PWU_NO_NEW_EXECUTION, :163-168). Every other state returns `{ok:true}`, PROPOSED included, because `isTerminalState('PWU.workLifecycleState','PROPOSED')` is false. Its docblock (execution.ts:144-147) cites RPH-PWU-010 / §8.3 only and never mentions PROPOSED. It is the SOLE predicate behind `pwuOpennessRefusal` (packages/rph-application/src/handlers/execution.ts:818-841, the openness call at :833), which is the openness gate for ActivateExecutionPlan (execution.ts:475) and, via execution.ts:736-737, for the six step commands that declare `pwuOpenness: 'REQUIRES_OPEN_PWU'` (packages/rph-domain/src/step-command-spec.ts:197, :220, :268, :291, :339, :385). PROPOSED, SHAPING and READY are all "not yet opened" rather than "open", and the predicate's default admits all three.

THE DRIVEN ARRANGEMENT (re-driven this pass; scratchpad/v4c_sta4_1.mjs under node, VERBATIM):
  CaptureIntent -> ACCEPTED
  ProposePwu -> ACCEPTED
  PWU workLifecycleState = PROPOSED
  ProposeExecutionPlan -> ACCEPTED
  ApproveExecutionPlan -> ACCEPTED
  ActivateExecutionPlan -> ACCEPTED
  StartExecutionStep (PWU still PROPOSED) -> ACCEPTED
  PWU workLifecycleState AFTER = PROPOSED
  step state = RUNNING
Nothing moves the PWU's axis, so the work runs and the governed record never says the unit executed.

THE CONTROL AT THE SAME PREDICATE, so the refusal machinery is shown alive (scratchpad/v4c_sta4_ctl.mjs, VERBATIM):
  canResumeExecutionOnPwu(PROPOSED) -> ok=true
  canResumeExecutionOnPwu(SHAPING) -> ok=true
  canResumeExecutionOnPwu(EXECUTING) -> ok=true
  canResumeExecutionOnPwu(BASELINED) -> ok=false | RPH_BASELINED_PWU_NO_RESUME | a baselined PWU requires a successor revision before new execution
  canResumeExecutionOnPwu(ABANDONED) -> ok=false | RPH_CLOSED_PWU_NO_NEW_EXECUTION | the PWU is ABANDONED, a terminal workLifecycleState — a closed unit of work opens no new execution
  canResumeExecutionOnPwu(SUPERSEDED) -> ok=false | RPH_CLOSED_PWU_NO_NEW_EXECUTION | …
  canResumeExecutionOnPwu(INVALIDATED) -> ok=true
  terminalStates = ["BASELINED","ABANDONED","SUPERSEDED"] ; isTerminalState PROPOSED = false
This is a MISSING LIMB, not a dead site: limb:STA-4:8 (baselined work) refuses at this exact function.

THE REMEDY. Give `canResumeExecutionOnPwu` a PROPOSED limb — better, invert it into an OPENNESS test naming the states that admit new execution, since the current "not terminal" default admits PROPOSED, SHAPING and READY alike, and STA-4's own sentence treats openness as a positive property. Refuse with its own reason string (not RPH-PWU-009's or RPH-PWU-010's), because the enforcement register deliberately keeps those two markers distinguishable (enforcement-register.ts:795-798) and a shared marker would let one arrangement satisfy three rules.

⚠ THE REMEDY REDDENS A COMMITTED SUITE AND THE ENTRY MUST SAY SO. packages/rph-application/src/handlers/execution-start-gate.test.ts's `beforeEach` (:174-208) captures an Intent and proposes a PWU and NEVER shapes it — the file contains 0 occurrences of BeginPwuShaping / ChangePwuState / workLifecycleState — so all 42 of its `it` blocks start steps against a PROPOSED PWU. The same arrangement recurs across ~20 other execution test files. The predicted red is a fixture change, not a regression, and a filing that omits it invites the next reader to "fix" the test instead of the guard.

NOTHING RECORDS IT. All four corpora searched by id and by site, with observed positive controls (see searchTranscript). filing_statement:
REG-F (new ordinal) — THE DE MINIMIS FLOOR IS A SET, NOT A SEQUENCE, AND IT FIRES AT TWO TRANSITIONS RATHER THAN AT EVERY MATERIAL ONE.

WHAT CANON REQUIRES. JPWB-DOC-003 §8.2 ASR-3 (canon line 249), limb 3 verbatim: "Every material professional transformation receives, in order: (1) strict output-contract validation plus applicable deterministic invariants; (2) identity, semantic-version, provenance, authority, and trace completeness checks; (3) a Reasoning Review Assessment when the transformation is produced or materially shaped by an AI/agent; (4) canonical admission/disposition and enforcement of the protected downstream transition." Two things beyond the shared floor SET are stated: SEQUENCING ("in order") and UNIVERSALITY ("every material professional transformation"). ASR-3's own SCOPE line makes materiality broad by default — "a result is material by default when it creates or changes professional content, supplies a downstream actor, proposes a Claim or Evidence, changes decomposition, contributes to a Decision/Baseline package, or supports a governed transition."

WHAT THE CODE DOES. (a) SEQUENCING IS NOT REPRESENTED. packages/rph-application/src/handlers/floor-gate.ts:20-24 declares `FLOOR_POLICY_IDS_REQUIRED` as a `const` array — a literal, not a branch — and the only predicate over it is `floorGateBlock` (floor-gate.ts:305-327), which is `FLOOR_POLICY_IDS_REQUIRED.map(...).filter((r) => r.disposition !== 'SATISFIED')`: an UNORDERED set-membership test that reports every non-SATISFIED policy at once. No site anywhere asks whether check (1) preceded (2), or (2) preceded (3); the refusal string names all three floor policies simultaneously (observed: REJECTED / '(floor.schema-invariant=MISSING, floor.identity-provenance=MISSING, floor.reasoning-review=MISSING)'). Sequencing is not merely unenforced — it is INEXPRESSIBLE to the gate, whose only datum per policy is a disposition.

(b) UNIVERSALITY REACHES TWO PROTECTED TRANSITIONS. `floorGateBlock` has exactly two production callers, measured (`grep -rn "floorGateBlock" --include=*.ts packages/ apps/ --exclude-dir=dist | grep -v "\.test\.ts"`): packages/rph-application/src/handlers/pwa-authoring.ts:966 (via `pwaFloorGate`, wired as the PublishPwa guard at :1002) and packages/rph-application/src/handlers/execution.ts:1432 (completeExecutionStep). Every other material transformation ASR-3's SCOPE enumerates — proposing a Claim or Evidence, changing decomposition, contributing to a Decision/Baseline package — reaches its own protected transition without the floor being consulted.

WHY THIS IS NOT ALREADY COVERED, verified in both directions. The corpus's floor material is about a THIRD property — whether the floor can be SWITCHED OFF. REG-F-202 / the floor-gate.ts:253-282 docblock delete the waiver-discharge apparatus (unconditionality). REG-F-024 (docs/canon/JPWB-REG-005:855-866) and docs/_working/DESIGN-floor-declared-scope.md fix the floor's DECLARED scope by OBJECT TYPE, and REG-005:865 states explicitly that `floor-gate.ts` "never reads `applicableObjectTypes` or `applicability` at all" — which settles universality over object types and says nothing about universality over TRANSFORMATIONS. `grep -rn -i "in order"` over all four corpora returns no floor-sequencing material; "repaired successor", "short-circuit" (in the ASR-3 sense) and "unordered" return nothing; verif/guard-enforcement-ledger.data.ts carries no floor or reasoning-review row at all.

THE REMEDY, stated so the implementer does not reach for the wrong one. Two separable acts, and the entry should say which is which. (i) SEQUENCING: canon states an ORDER; the gate carries a SET. Either the order is made expressible — the floor record acquires a stage/precedence so `floorGateBlock` can refuse an out-of-order admission — or, if the sponsor rules that the four steps are a conjunction whose order is immaterial at the gate (deterministic failure may short-circuit, per ASR-3's next sentence), then that ruling must be RECORDED, because today the order is silently dropped rather than deliberately waived. (ii) UNIVERSALITY: the floor's two call sites must be measured against ASR-3's SCOPE enumeration and each uncovered material transformation either gated or disclosed by name. ⚠ Do NOT cite REG-F-024 as prior art for (ii): its subject is `applicableObjectTypes`, and its own finding is that the gate ignores that field entirely.

REG-F (new ordinal) — A BASELINE IS PROMOTED OVER AN INVALIDATED PWU UNDER THE ASSESSMENT THAT CONCLUDED BEFORE THE INVALIDATION: THE LIMB'S 'WITHOUT REASSESSMENT' QUALIFIER HAS NO READER, AND NO FIELD COULD CARRY ONE.

WHAT CANON REQUIRES. JPWB-DOC-003 §6 STA-7, limb 2 verbatim: "An invalidated or semantically changed satisfied PWU cannot be baselined without reassessment."

WHAT IS ALREADY ENFORCED AND MUST NOT BE FILED, stated first so the entry is not read wider than it is. (A) The bare prohibition "INVALIDATED … cannot be baselined" IS enforced at two independent sites, each with a discriminating control. Site 1, the named command: after `InvalidatePwu` ACCEPTED (source SATISFIED), `BaselinePwu` -> REJECTED | RPH_ILLEGAL_STATE_TRANSITION | "BaselinePwu does not declare INVALIDATED as a source state — it claims [SATISFIED, RECOMPOSED] for BASELINED. This is an UNDECLARED ARROW … (REG-F-114)."; CONTROL, byte-identical with the invalidation omitted -> ACCEPTED, PWU reaches BASELINED. Site 2, the generic setter: `ChangePwuState INVALIDATED -> BASELINED` -> REJECTED | RPH_ILLEGAL_STATE_TRANSITION | "not a legal PWU.workLifecycleState transition: INVALIDATED -> BASELINED" (pwuGuards.ts:164 over transitions.data.ts:621, the illegal row `{from:'INVALIDATED', to:'BASELINED', reason:'§8.3 — must be rejected.'}`); its CONTROL, `ChangePwuState SATISFIED -> BASELINED`, refuses DIFFERENTLY (RPH_INVARIANT_VIOLATION, "that arrow belongs to BaselinePwu"), which is what proves site 2 discriminates on LEGALITY rather than blanket-refusing every ->BASELINED setter call. (B) Upstream SEMANTIC-CHANGE staleness IS enforced at packages/rph-application/src/handlers/governance.ts:965 (STALE_DECISION_VERSION).

WHAT IS ALSO ALREADY FILED AND MUST BE CITED RATHER THAN RE-FOUND. The ITEM-LIFECYCLE half — a PWU sitting in INVALIDATED being frozen into an AUTHORITATIVE Baseline through `PromoteBaseline` — is RPH-PWU-008 (packages/rph-domain/src/enforcement-register.ts:2122-2150, kind UNENFORCED_DISCLOSED, guard.kind OBSERVED_ADMISSION), whose `why` is that "`promoteBaseline` builds its candidate item set from the COMMAND PAYLOAD (`expectedItemObjectVersions`) … and calls `ctx.store.loadObject` on no item at all." ⚠ Its canonAnchor is STA-4's "invalidated work cannot be baselined", a NEIGHBOURING invariant, so nothing files it under STA-7.

THE RESIDUAL THIS ENTRY IS FOR — THE 'WITHOUT REASSESSMENT' QUALIFIER, WHICH RPH-PWU-008 DOES NOT REACH. RPH-PWU-008's organ is the ITEM set (never loaded). This defect's organ is the ASSESSMENT set, which IS loaded and IS checked — and checked on the wrong axis.
SITE: `promoteBaseline` builds its required-assessment view at packages/rph-application/src/handlers/governance.ts:901-913, mapping `p.requiredAssessmentIds` — THE CALLER'S OWN PAYLOAD — and loading each assessment only to read `assessmentState`, yielding `{ assessmentId, complete, disposition }` (:913). That is the whole of `RequiredAssessmentView` (packages/rph-domain/src/governance.ts:195-200 — three fields, NONE temporal), and `findAssessmentDefects` (packages/rph-domain/src/governance.ts:324-341) tests only `!a.complete` and `!PROMOTABLE_DISPOSITIONS.has(a.disposition)` where `PROMOTABLE_DISPOSITIONS = new Set(['SATISFIED','WAIVED'])` (:261). So "assessed SINCE the invalidating event" is not merely unchecked — it is INEXPRESSIBLE to the check, and the set to be checked is the caller's to nominate. That doubles the defect: the caller chooses the assessments AND no field could record their recency.

THE DRIVEN ARRANGEMENT (scratchpad/rf-sta72.mjs, node, verbatim). The required ASSESS was completed while the PWU was SATISFIED at semanticVersion 1. `InvalidatePwu` (the real command, source SATISFIED) -> ACCEPTED; PWU workLifecycleState = INVALIDATED, semanticVersion = 1; the assessment still reads SATISFIED, having concluded BEFORE the invalidation. THE ADMISSION: `PromoteBaseline` over the INVALIDATED PWU under that PRE-invalidation assessment -> **ACCEPTED**; Baseline status AUTHORITATIVE; items `[{"objectId":"pwu_01ARZ3NDEKTSV4RRFFQ69G5QP0","semanticVersion":1}]`; item PWU workLifecycleState still = INVALIDATED. No post-invalidation reassessment was demanded of any party.
TWO CONTROLS, BOTH DISCRIMINATING, both built while the co-subject was still at v1 so neither is an ordering artefact: (a) `PromoteBaseline` with NOTHING moved -> ACCEPTED, baseline AUTHORITATIVE — the chain is promotable; (b) with the promotion decision's co-subject INTENT genuinely revised 1->2 after `ApproveDecision`, `PromoteBaseline` -> REJECTED | RPH_INVARIANT_VIOLATION | "Cannot promote baseline bsl_…MB0: STALE_DECISION_VERSION — the promotion decision dec_…MD0 bound subject version(s) no longer current (int_…W00 approved@1 current@2); the subject is re-review-required (RPH-GOV-003)." So the site DOES refuse on VERSION staleness and does NOT refuse on ASSESSMENT staleness — the discrimination is exactly on the limb's qualifier. SIBLING CONTROL AT THE SAME HANDLER, proving the site is alive and polices invalidation of a DIFFERENT object type: the byte-identical promotion whose decision considered an INVALIDATED Evidence -> REJECTED | RPH_EVIDENCE_INVALIDATED.

⚠ ONE MEASURED BOUND CARRIED SO THE ENTRY IS NOT OVER-READ. A PWU's OWN `semanticVersion` cannot move — only intent.ts:329 and decomposition.ts:495 pass `bumpSemanticVersion: true`, and the PWU sat at 1 throughout the drive — so the literal "semantically changed PWU" arrangement is unreachable and the driven one moves an upstream co-subject instead. REG-005:3158 (REG-F-109) already records "a PWU's semanticVersion is 1 forever — CORRECTED: because the PWU shape is WRITE-ONCE by ratified design"; the entry should CITE it rather than re-find it.

THE REMEDY. `RequiredAssessmentView` must acquire a temporal or causal field (the assessment's conclusion time, or the version/lifecycle event it concluded against), and `findAssessmentDefects` must gain an arm refusing an assessment that concluded before the subject's most recent invalidating or version-raising event. Separately — and this is the half RPH-BAS-004's own `declaredMutations` already names as an evasion ("the required set is whatever the PromoteBaseline payload lists in `requiredAssessmentIds`. A promotion listing NONE passes this arm vacuously") — the required-assessment set must be DERIVED from the baseline's frozen items and their applicable policies rather than nominated by the promoter. ⚠ CONJUNCT (b) — "and preserves its attempt history" — HOLDS, DRIVEN, AND MUST NOT BE FILED. After Start -> Fail -> Retry -> Start and then `SupersedeExecutionPlan`, the superseded plan's events read ["ExecutionPlanProposed","ExecutionPlanApproved","ExecutionPlanActivated","ExecutionStepStarted","ExecutionStepFailed","ExecutionStepRetried","ExecutionStepStarted"] before and the same seven plus "ExecutionPlanSuperseded" after; `steps[]` untouched. CONJUNCT (a) — "Plan revision SUPERSEDES the prior plan" — IS THE DIVERGENCE, AND NOTHING COMPELS IT.

WHAT THE CODE DOES. Nothing requires a successor plan to supersede the plan it replaces. `plan-proposal.ts` has ZERO references to `workUnitId` (positive control: 17 references to `steps` in the same file), and `proposeExecutionPlan`'s only cross-object check is that `workUnitId` resolves to a PROFESSIONAL_WORK_UNIT (execution.ts:287-295). REG-F (new ordinal) — OMITTING ONE OPTIONAL PAYLOAD FIELD SKIPS THE ENTIRE TYPE-IDENTITY BINDING GATE, AND THE EVENT THEN ASSERTS A DECLARATION NOBODY MADE.

WHAT CANON REQUIRES. JPWB-DOC-003 §4 OBJ-3, limb 3 verbatim: "Kind or label fields (`pwuKind` and its relatives) are descriptive discriminators, never type identity: type identity resolves by binding to a versioned PWA or a declared local extension." Its WHY, verbatim: "kind-as-identity lets an unversioned string impersonate a governed type." The clause is unqualified — type identity resolves by ONE OF TWO DISJUNCTS, always.

WHAT THE CODE DOES — three sites, one gate.
(a) THE OPT-OUT. packages/rph-application/src/handlers/pwu.ts:193, first statement of `rejectInvalidOwnershipBinding`: `if (!p.undertakingId) return undefined;` (`grep -c -F` -> resolves exactly once). It returns before any binding check. `undertakingId` is `z.string().optional()` on `ProposePwuPayloadSchema` (packages/rph-contracts/src/messages.ts:132), so ANY caller opts out of the whole RPH-CON-009 binding guard by omitting one optional field.
(b) THE INFERENCE FROM ABSENCE. packages/rph-application/src/handlers/pwu.ts:353: `isLocalExtension: p.isLocalExtension ?? p.pwuTypeId === undefined,` on the emitted `PwuProposed` payload. The limb requires a DECLARED local extension; on this path the declaration is INFERRED from a missing field. That is an OBJ-1 inference-from-absence sitting inside OBJ-3's own second disjunct.
(c) THE OBJECT CANNOT CARRY WHAT THE EVENT ASSERTS. packages/rph-application/src/handlers/pwu.ts:322: `...(p.isLocalExtension !== undefined ? { isLocalExtension: p.isLocalExtension } : {}),` — the object writer records the field ONLY when the payload supplied it. So the governed stream asserts `isLocalExtension: true` while the authoritative object carries no such field for a downstream reader to consult.

THE DRIVEN ARRANGEMENT (full chain through Engine.dispatch). ENFORCED HALF, so this is a missing limb and not a dead guard: with an Undertaking bound, `ProposePwu{undertakingId set, isLocalExtension:false, NO pwuTypeId, pwuKind:'PRODUCT_REALIZATION'}` -> REJECTED | RPH_VALIDATION_SEMANTIC_FAILED | "ProposePwu: a non-local PWU Instance must name a pwuTypeId that resolves to a PWU Type in the Undertaking's bound PWA — pwuKind alone is insufficient (RPH-CON-009). Set isLocalExtension=true for an Undertaking-local extension." CONTROL 1 (the versioned-PWA disjunct): identical command plus a valid `pwuTypeId` -> ACCEPTED. CONTROL 2 (the declared-local-extension disjunct): identical command with `isLocalExtension:true` and no `pwuTypeId` -> ACCEPTED. SIBLING PROOF THE SITE DISCRIMINATES ON VERSION: a type from a second PWA at version 9.9.9 -> REJECTED | "ProposePwu: pwuTypeId pwut_… does not resolve to a PWU Type in the Undertaking's bound PWA pwa_… @ 1.0.0 (RPH-CON-009)."
THE ADMISSION: `ProposePwu` with NO `undertakingId`, NO `pwuTypeId`, NO `isLocalExtension`, and `pwuKind: 'TOTALLY_INVENTED_KIND_NOT_IN_ANY_PWA'` -> **ACCEPTED**. Stored object ownership fields: `{"pwuKind":"TOTALLY_INVENTED_KIND_NOT_IN_ANY_PWA"}` AND NOTHING ELSE — `Object.hasOwn(state,'isLocalExtension') === false`, `pwuTypeId` undefined, `undertakingId` undefined. On that object type identity resolves by NEITHER disjunct and an unversioned free string is the only type-ish field it carries: canon's WHY, verbatim. The emitted `PwuProposed` payload, read back from the log: `{"pwuId":"pwu_01ARZ3NDEKTSV4RRFFQ69G5FB5","isLocalExtension":true,"pwuKind":"TOTALLY_INVENTED_KIND_NOT_IN_ANY_PWA",…}` — the `true` inferred at :353 from an absence.
REPORTED AS A CONJUNCT, NOT SCORED AS THE VIOLATION: with a valid `pwuTypeId` bound, `ProposePwu` with `pwuKind:'ARCHITECTURE_DEFINITION'` against a PWU Type whose `pwuKind` is `'PRODUCT_REALIZATION'` -> ACCEPTED; instance kind and bound-type kind disagree and nothing reconciles them. Consistent with kind being merely descriptive, but it means the instance's kind string is anchored to nothing versioned.

WHAT THE NEVER-CLAUSE SURVIVES, recorded because it dissolves a larger finding. `pwuKind` is genuinely never used AS type identity elsewhere: packages/rph-engine/src/governing-policies.ts:33-72 passes it only as a SUBJECT ATTRIBUTE into `policyApplicability` (it FILTERS an already-declared policy set, never SELECTS one); packages/rph-domain/src/governance.ts:735-736's `pwuKindConditions` is an allow-list narrowing applicability; packages/rph-projections/src/compatibility-view.ts:50's `milestoneForKind` maps kind to a legacy phase label the file itself calls "a viewer's familiar phase, never authoritative state." All three are descriptive-discriminator uses the limb permits. The defect is the STANDALONE PATH only.

The only prior art is a WORKING PAPER deferral, not a register finding: docs/_working/HARMONIZATION-LOG.md PART 3t ('Increment 35'), section "`undertakingId` — deferred, with the reason" (:2790-2795) — "It goes live the moment the standalone reference drive becomes a real Undertaking (its own increment: bootstrap a minimal published PWA + Undertaking, mirroring seed-workbench, then make `undertakingId`/`isLocalExtension` *required* on the ProposePwu **command** too — fixing the §11.2 contract-drift in the same pass)." It asserts the exemption is CORRECT and states no gap. REG-F-<next> - `coverageClaims` is a governed field of the DECOMPOSITION_CONTRACT that nothing reads: a contract can reach VALID carrying a COMPLETE coverage claim over an obligation that was never asserted and a child that is not among its own children, and the engine publishes that claim in the governed record.

WHAT CANON REQUIRES. JPWB-DOC-003 §6 DEC-2, limb 8 (anchor_line 215): a decomposition records "coverage claims and validation status". DEC-2's first sentence makes a decomposition an ASSERTION about how the parent's work is covered; the coverage claim is the field in which that assertion is made checkable.

WHAT THE CODE DOES. `coverageClaims` is optional on `ProposeDecomposition` (`packages/rph-contracts/src/messages.ts:465`), required on the object (`packages/rph-contracts/src/objects.ts:638`), and defaulted to `[]` at `packages/rph-application/src/handlers/decomposition.ts:67`. A repo-wide census - `grep -rn --include=*.ts --include=*.svelte -F 'coverageClaims' packages/ apps/ verif/ scripts/` minus node_modules, dist and .svelte-kit - returns SIX lines: two writes (decomposition.ts:67 and :103) and four schema declarations. ZERO READERS. Neither `claimId`, `parentObligationIds`, `childWorkUnitIds`, `coverageType` nor `rationale` is ever resolved, and no validation path consults the array. The claimed rph-domain "coverage-gate" is a different subject: `packages/rph-domain/src/decomposition.ts:183,194` implement per-relevant-child coverage of CONSTRAINT PROPAGATIONS (§11.2 / Property P3), never a CoverageClaim.

THE DRIVEN ARRANGEMENT (node, real engine). A contract proposed with:
  coverageClaims: [{claimId:'clm_ghost', parentObligationIds:['obl_never_asserted'], childWorkUnitIds:['pwu_not_a_child'], coverageType:'COMPLETE', rationale:'fabricated'}]
  ProposeDecomposition -> ACCEPTED
  ValidateDecomposition{VALID} -> ACCEPTED ; contract status after = VALID
  stored state reads back BYTE FOR BYTE: [{"claimId":"clm_ghost","parentObligationIds":["obl_never_asserted"],"childWorkUnitIds":["pwu_not_a_child"],"coverageType":"COMPLETE","rationale":"fabricated"}]
Omission is admitted just as freely: `ValidateDecomposition{VALID}` with `coverageClaims` OMITTED -> ACCEPTED, status VALID, stored `coverageClaims = []`.

THE CONTROL, IN THE SAME RUN, ON THE SAME COMMAND (proving the validation gate is alive and simply never inspects the claim): the byte-adjacent twin with a constraint dispositioned for one child only -> REJECTED | RPH_INVARIANT_VIOLATION | "ValidateDecomposition cannot mark dcp_... valid: the decomposition does not conserve its parent's obligations/constraints (§35.1 / RPH-DEC-002/007 / RPH-CNS-001..004): SILENT_CONSTRAINT_DROP(con_...->pwu_...)". The guard fires on the obligation/constraint fields and never looks at the coverage claim.

WHY THIS IS WORSE THAN THE ORDINARY HOLLOW-FIELD CASE. OBJ-7 states "a governed object that nothing consults is a defect, not documentation"; here it is a governed FIELD, and the field is the one that would make DEC-2's own first sentence checkable. The engine does not merely ignore the claim - it PUBLISHES it in the authoritative record, so a downstream reader (or a future gate) can read a fabricated COMPLETE coverage assertion off canonical state.

TWO TRAPS FOR THE REMEDY, BOTH ALREADY DEMONSTRATED IN THIS REPOSITORY, AND THE ENTRY MUST NAME THEM.
(i) A census asserting "every VALID contract carries at least one coverage claim" is satisfiable by ONE EMPTY CLAIM - the REG-F-028 shape. The check must be on the CONTENT, not the cardinality.
(ii) The check must RESOLVE `parentObligationIds` against the PARENT's `obligationIds` and `childWorkUnitIds` against THIS contract's own `childWorkUnitIds`. The latter resolution is itself absent (it is limb:DEC-2:1's subject, which sits on the UNENFORCED_OBSERVED_ADMISSION arm), so the two should be SEQUENCED - a coverage check written over unresolved child ids would certify against a set that is itself unchecked.

REMEDY. Resolve the claim inside `validateDecomposition`: refuse VALID when a claim names an obligation absent from the parent's `obligationIds`, or a child absent from this contract's `childWorkUnitIds`, or declares `coverageType: 'COMPLETE'` over a proper subset. Red-first: the `clm_ghost` arrangement above must become a refusal, with the SILENT_CONSTRAINT_DROP control still firing on its own limb (so the new refusal is proved distinguishable from the existing one) and a well-formed coverage claim still ACCEPTED.

REG-F (new ordinal) — 'SUPERSEDED BY A STRONGER CONSTRAINT' IS A TRUTHINESS TEST ON A STRING: NEITHER THE REPLACEMENT'S EXISTENCE NOR ITS STRENGTH IS CHECKED.

SCOPE OF THIS ENTRY — ONE CLAUSE OF THE LIMB ONLY. limb:DEC-4:5 welds two things: "or superseded by a stronger constraint" (a disposition ALTERNATIVE) and "No silent omission" (a GENERAL PROHIBITION over all five alternatives). The second is ENFORCED AND FILED and nothing is owed for it — RPH-DEC-003 (packages/rph-domain/src/enforcement-register.ts:3656-3672, kind ENFORCED, canonAnchor 'No silent omission; no unauthorized weakening', refusalMarker 'SILENT_CONSTRAINT_DROP(') — and it was re-driven green at two acts this pass. The entry must say so, or a reader will take the whole limb as broken. (Recorded against the split rule w3b-limb-split/1.0.0: the two clauses score oppositely and a future split should separate them.)

WHAT CANON REQUIRES. JPWB-DOC-003 §6 DEC-4 (Constraint exhaustive disposition) permits SUPERSESSION only "by a STRONGER constraint". The kernel's own docblock states the check as if it existed — packages/rph-domain/src/decomposition.ts:163, verbatim: " *   - SUPERSEDED requires the id of the stronger replacement constraint."

WHAT THE CODE DOES. packages/rph-domain/src/decomposition.ts:232-235, `checkConstraintDisposition`'s SUPERSEDED arm, entire: `case 'SUPERSEDED': if (!r.supersededByConstraintId) out.push({ code: 'SUPERSEDED_WITHOUT_REPLACEMENT', constraintId }); break;`. It tests the TRUTHINESS of a string. Neither the EXISTENCE of the replacement nor its STRENGTH is examined. packages/rph-application/src/handlers/decomposition.ts:257 — `buildConstraintInput` passes `supersededByConstraintId: r.supersededByConstraintId` straight through from the caller's payload.

THE ASYMMETRY THAT MAKES THIS A REG-F-014/REG-F-102 INSTANCE AND NOT A DESIGN CHOICE, AND IT IS SEVEN LINES AWAY IN THE SAME FUNCTION. At packages/rph-application/src/handlers/decomposition.ts:243-249 the NEIGHBOURING field on the SAME disposition record, `authorityDecisionId`, IS resolved: `const authorityBasis = (id) => { if (!id) return undefined; const stored = ctx.store.loadObject(id); if (stored?.objectType !== 'DECISION') return undefined; const parsed = DecisionObjectSchema.safeParse(stored.state); return parsed.success && parsed.data.status === 'EFFECTIVE' ? id : undefined; }` — under REG-F-102 — and an unresolvable id is passed on as ABSENT so the kernel's finding fires. `supersededByConstraintId` (:257) gets none of that.

THE DRIVEN ARRANGEMENT (scratchpad/v4b_dec4.mjs, node, controls in the same run).
- S8b: CON strength = MANDATORY, CON2 strength = ADVISORY; a MANDATORY applicable parent constraint dispositioned SUPERSEDED by the real but strictly WEAKER CON2 -> ValidateDecomposition VALID -> ACCEPTED | contract status = VALID.
- S8c: the same constraint dispositioned SUPERSEDED by the literal string 'nothing-at-all', which resolves to no object at all -> ProposeDecomposition ACCEPTED -> ValidateDecomposition VALID -> ACCEPTED | contract status = VALID.
- THREE CONTROLS, ALL REFUSING AT THE SAME SITE: S8 (SUPERSEDED with an EMPTY replacement) -> REJECTED | RPH_INVARIANT_VIOLATION | SUPERSEDED_WITHOUT_REPLACEMENT(con_…D03); S2 (a relevant child left undispositioned) -> REJECTED | SILENT_CONSTRAINT_DROP(con_…D03->pwu_…D0B), contract status UNDER_REVIEW; S8d (the SIBLING FIELD, same command, same record, the same dangling literal 'nothing-at-all' as an AUTHORITY) -> REFUSED. 'nothing-at-all' as an authority is refused; 'nothing-at-all' as a superseding constraint is accepted and the contract reaches VALID.

AGGRAVATING FACT THE FILING MUST CARRY. The suite's ONLY SUPERSEDED case pins the hole in place: packages/rph-domain/src/decomposition.test.ts:321-329 supplies `disposition: 'SUPERSEDED', supersededByConstraintId: 'con_stronger'` — an id naming no object, its strength asserted only by its NAME — and asserts `expect(r.ok).toBe(true)`. Green today, green after any repair that resolves the id, so the repair needs its own red first.

evidence:
THE LIMB'S TWO HALVES SEPARATE, AND I SCORE THEM SEPARATELY RATHER THAN AVERAGING THEM.

HALF ONE — 'IS A NAMED FAILURE MODE' — HOLDS, AND NOT ONLY IN CANON. The lane brief anticipated that the only naming might be canon itself; measured, it is not. The failure mode is named three times in SHIPPED PRODUCTION DATA (packages/rph-product-realization-pwa/src/ontology.data.ts:624, :1589, :2586), each with a DOC-004 §9.1 FindingDefinition carrying name, description, defaultSeverity and an authored severityRationale; the mapping from canon's exact wording to the code is recorded in the corpus itself (ontology.data.ts:126 quotes 'scope expansion disguised as helpfulness' verbatim as the INTAKE template's source; JPWB-REG-005:4466 maps that phrase to UNAUTHORIZED_SCOPE_EXPANSION). And I did not stop at reading the literals: I stood up a real engine, seeded the policy library, and LOADED the three policies out of the store — all three ACTIVE, with the codes present and CHILD_INTENT_DIVERGENCE graded BLOCKING. The naming is also GATED: doc004-conformance.test.ts:296 machine-checks every policy's findingTypes against the ratified DOC-004 body with an exact toEqual, and seed-finding-definitions.test.ts:130-137 pins pol_intent_fidelity's seven codes as a literal list. Deleting the name is not a silent act. So this half is a real, observable, defended artifact, and calling the whole limb UNENFORCED_NO_SHAPE would be false — the shape exists and I held it in my hand.

HALF TWO — 'NOT A VIRTUE' — IS CARRIED BY NOTHING, AND THE NAME IS INERT. Three measurements, each with its own positive control:
  (i) Nothing READS the field the name lives in. findingDefinitions has 23 non-test occurrences and not one is a decision read; its five-lines-away sibling requiredEvidence, on the same object, written by the same handler, IS read by Gate A at assurance.ts:1324/:1338.
  (ii) Nothing PRODUCES either code. The only site that can mint CHILD_INTENT_DIVERGENCE is packages/rph-domain/src/decomposition.ts:557, inside a composition no non-test file imports; its neighbour forty lines up, MISSING_OBLIGATION_ALLOCATION at :82, IS called and I observed its output in a live refusal message while scoring limb 1.
  (iii) The wire does not CHECK the name. Driven: against a policy declaring exactly one code, both 'CHILD_INTENT_DIVERGENCE' and the invented 'BANANA_NOT_A_FAILURE_MODE' were accepted and stored verbatim. A vocabulary that admits a word I made up is a label, not a control.
So the engine's actual disposition toward scope expansion is neither 'failure mode' nor 'virtue' — it is silence, which is the condition the limb's 'not a virtue' clause exists to rule out.

WHY PARTIAL_DIVERGENT_FILED AND NOT SOMETHING ELSE. Not ENFORCED_BY_CONSTRUCTION: the drive proves the opposite of schema-closure — the finding vocabulary is an OPEN z.string(), so nothing makes the name load-bearing. Not UNENFORCED_NO_SHAPE: the shape exists as ACTIVE governed objects and is test-gated. Not UNENFORCED_DEAD_PREDICATE: there is no predicate here at all, only data (the dead predicate belongs to limb 1 and is scored there). Not DIVERGENT_UNFILED: the divergence — 'nothing consumes those types except a seeder' — is recorded verbatim in the enforcement register, under the row whose canonAnchor is DEC-5's own sentence, and that record is behaviourally gated by a test I ran green today. PARTIAL_DIVERGENT_FILED is the honest arm: half the limb is discharged by a real artifact I observed, half is discharged by nothing, and the gap between them is already on the record.

filing_statement:
WHAT CANON REQUIRES. JPWB-DOC-003 §6 DEC-5, line 227, limb 2: "Scope expansion disguised as helpfulness is a named failure mode, not a virtue."

⚠ DO NOT FILE THE NAMING HALF AS A GAP — IT IS REAL AND DEFENDED, and a filer who reads only the inertness paragraphs will get this wrong. Loaded live out of a seeded engine (createEngine + seedPolicyLibrary, then store.loadObject): `pol_intent_fidelity` ACTIVE with 7 findingDefinitions including UNAUTHORIZED_SCOPE_EXPANSION | MATERIAL | "Unauthorized scope expansion"; `pol_decomposition_coverage` ACTIVE with 10 including CHILD_INTENT_DIVERGENCE | BLOCKING; `pol_intent_preservation` ACTIVE with 8 including INTENT_EXPANSION | MATERIAL. The naming is also GATED: doc004-conformance.test.ts:296 machine-checks every policy's findingTypes against the ratified DOC-004 body with an exact `toEqual`, and seed-finding-definitions.test.ts:130-137 pins pol_intent_fidelity's seven codes as a literal list (both run green: 'Test Files 2 passed (2) / Tests 131 passed (131)'). THE FILING IS ABOUT INERTNESS, NOT ABSENCE.

WHAT THE CODE DOES — the second clause, "not a virtue", is carried by nothing, measured at three layers each with its own observed control.
(i) NOTHING READS THE FIELD THE NAME LIVES IN. `findingDefinitions` has 23 non-test occurrences across packages/, apps/ and verif/ and not one is a decision read; the writer is packages/rph-application/src/handlers/assurance.ts:219. OBSERVED CONTROL: its sibling on the same object, written FIVE LINES AWAY at assurance.ts:214, `policy.requiredEvidence`, IS read twice and both reads are Gate A of `completeAssuranceAssessment` (assurance.ts:1324 `const requiredEvidenceIds = (policy.requiredEvidence ?? [])`, :1338 `const blockingEvidenceIds = (policy.requiredEvidence ?? [])`). One governs; the other does not.
(ii) NOTHING PRODUCES THE CODE. The only site that can mint CHILD_INTENT_DIVERGENCE is packages/rph-domain/src/decomposition.ts:557, inside a composition no non-test file imports; UNAUTHORIZED_SCOPE_EXPANSION and INTENT_EXPANSION have NO minting site at all — every non-test occurrence is catalog data or register prose. OBSERVED CONTROL: MISSING_OBLIGATION_ALLOCATION, same file 475 lines up at decomposition.ts:82, IS a live emitter and its output was observed inside a real CommandResult.
(iii) THE WIRE DOES NOT CHECK THE NAME. SITE: packages/rph-contracts/src/messages.ts:355 — `findingCode: z.string().optional()` on RecordAssuranceObservationPayloadSchema, checked against nothing anywhere.

THE DRIVEN ARRANGEMENT (node, through Engine.dispatch). Against an ACTIVE ASSURANCE_POLICY whose `findingDefinitions` declares EXACTLY ONE code, 'UNFIT', with an assessment requested and begun under it, `RecordAssuranceObservation` accepts and stores VERBATIM: (a) 'UNFIT', in vocabulary [ACCEPTANCE CONTROL] -> ACCEPTED; (b) 'UNAUTHORIZED_SCOPE_EXPANSION', canon's own code and NOT in this policy's vocabulary -> ACCEPTED; (c) 'BANANA_NOT_A_FAILURE_MODE', a word invented for the probe [NONSENSE CONTROL] -> ACCEPTED. Read back: OB3/OB1/OB2.findingCode = UNFIT / CHILD_INTENT_DIVERGENCE / BANANA_NOT_A_FAILURE_MODE. REFUSAL CONTROL ON THE SAME COMMAND, proving the seam does refuse: `severity: 'NOT_A_SEVERITY'` -> VALIDATION_FAILED | RPH_VALIDATION_SCHEMA_FAILED. A vocabulary that admits an invented word is a label, not a control. So the engine's actual disposition toward scope expansion is neither "failure mode" nor "virtue" — it is SILENCE, which is the condition this clause exists to rule out.

WHY NOTHING RECORDS IT, and why this entry must be written AGAINST an existing entry rather than beside it. JPWB-REG-005:4463 REG-F-190 — CLOSED 2026-08-15, "AN OWED ITEM CLOSED AS A NON-ISSUE" — closes REG-F-185's owed item on exactly this ground: "✅ ALL SIX HAVE FINDING-CODE COVERAGE, ACROSS THE SEEDED POLICY SET … scope expansion disguised as helpfulness → `UNAUTHORIZED_SCOPE_EXPANSION` … there they are, among 99 finding codes over twelve policies." ITS REASONING IS RIGHT AND ITS CONCLUSION DOES NOT FOLLOW: presence of a code in a seeded policy establishes that the failure mode is NAMED; it does not establish that anything is done about it, and REG-F-190 never asks. THE ONLY OTHER RECORD IS A NEAR MISS FOR A NEIGHBOURING SUBJECT: packages/rph-domain/src/enforcement-register.ts:3492, inside RPH-DEC-004 (row opens :3477, canonAnchor "A child PWU introducing work beyond parent intent without authorization is a divergence"), carries "the seeded POL-DECOMPOSITION-COVERAGE policy lists CHILD_INTENT_DIVERGENCE among its finding types and nothing consumes those types except a seeder" — DEC-5's OTHER sentence, a different code, in a different policy, used as a supporting absence for a different claim.

WHAT THE FILING MUST ASK FOR.
(a) THAT REG-F-190's CLOSURE BE REOPENED OR NARROWED to what it actually measured: the six failure modes are NAMED in the seeded policy set; whether the names are load-bearing was not asked and is answered NO.
(b) A VOCABULARY GATE AT `RecordAssuranceObservation` — the cheapest item and the one that would have reddened the nonsense control: the subject assessment resolves to a policy, that policy carries `findingDefinitions`; refuse a `findingCode` the governing policy does not declare. That makes every name in the catalog load-bearing at one site.
(c) A CONSUMER FOR `findingDefinitions` AT ALL — the hollow-governed-layer shape: 99 codes across 12 policies, severity-graded, doc-conformance-checked and seeded into ACTIVE governed objects, and no decision reads the field.

NOT SHARED. Specifically NOT with limb:DEC-2:3 (whose subject is the DecompositionContract's obligation to RECORD rationale and intent mappings), and NOT closed by RPH-DEC-004, which is already filed for the child-scope sentence and whose remedy is the decomposition composition, not the observation vocabulary.

So the question is whether the plane EXISTS, and the answer is: a shape for it exists in the kernel, the plane itself does not, and BOTH facts are already recorded in committed, gated files. Hence PARTIAL_DIVERGENT_FILED rather than UNENFORCED_NO_SHAPE (there IS a shape) and rather than DIVERGENT_UNFILED (it IS filed).

THE HALF THAT EXISTS. packages/rph-domain/src/presentation.ts declares the plane in so many words: `PresentationBearing extends SemanticSnapshot { readonly revision: number; readonly layout?: unknown }` (:13-16), and `applyPresentationChange` (:38-43) returns `{ ...obj, revision: obj.revision + 1, layout: newLayout }` under the docblock 'swap the layout and bump the DISPLAY revision, leaving semanticVersion and assuranceState untouched'. Triage §3: presentation/introspection helpers are not governance rules.' }` and `isPresentationOnlyChange: { kind: 'DEAD_BY_DESIGN', why: 'Presentation function, as above. The INV-6 semantic-version rule it relates to is enforced in the handlers by comparing raw payload fields.' }`. No object schema carries a `layout` field (0 of 31; control 24 of 31 carry semanticVersion). No `presentationRevision` field exists anywhere in the repo. So there is no persisted layout to version, and therefore no revision plane for it.

THE FINDING THE FILINGS DO NOT YET CARRY — and it is the sharpest thing in this row. The kernel's 'own plane' is named `revision`, which is the SAME NAME as the store's optimistic-concurrency aggregate revision (packages/rph-persistence/src/schema.ts:74, sqlite-storage-adapter.ts:26/166/181, EnvelopeSchema `revision: RevisionSchema` at envelopes.ts:54) — the counter that EVERY semantic write bumps and that PER-4's `expectedRevision` check reads. I drove that to be sure of it rather than inferring it from the field name: five consecutive ACCEPTED semantic commands walked the Intent's store revision 0->1->2->3->4->5. So `applyPresentationChange` bumping `revision` would move the SEMANTIC concurrency plane, which is the precise arrangement 'layout has its OWN revision plane' exists to prevent. It is harmless only because the function is dead and never reaches the store. That collision is filed nowhere.

ARGUING THE FILING QUESTION THE LANE BRIEF ASKED (is the register note a FILING, or merely an observation?). FILING. Four reasons. (i) The audit's own arm definition names enforcement-register.ts as a filing venue and admits even 'a docblock that states the gap'; a typed field in a committed register is strictly stronger than a docblock. (ii) The note is not a passing remark about document drift — its second clause is a claim about the REPOSITORY ('the plane this repository does not have'), and it quotes the canon clause verbatim so the filing cannot drift from what it files against. (iii) It is not alone: RPH-PRJ-004's `why` body states the same absence independently and with the mechanism ('no `presentationRevision` field exists anywhere, so canon's "Layout has its own revision plane" describes a plane this repository has not built'), and then states the residue in the register's own voice ('THE RESIDUE IS THE SAME AS RPH-CON-008's: the day layout IS persisted, this rule becomes live with a real subject and nothing here would notice. It is satisfied by absence, which is not the same as enforced.'). (iv) The corroborating filing is GATED, which is what makes the gap unable to vanish silently: verif/dead-kernel-census.test.ts's header states 'Wiring one reddens this file (delete its row). Adding a new uncalled kernel function reddens this file' — so the day anyone wires `applyPresentationChange`, that file turns red and the disposition must be re-argued. THE HONEST COUNTER, recorded rather than suppressed: the note sits in `canonCarriage.note`, whose declared job is describing how canon carries the ratified statement, and the register's disposition for RPH-PRJ-004 is NOT_A_COMMAND_REFUSAL rather than a disclosure — so a reader could call it an observation about the DOCUMENTS. This row is therefore NOT a DIVERGENT_UNFILED.

Two contract types exist and both are semantic (DECOMPOSITION_CONTRACT, RECOMPOSITION_CONTRACT); none is presentational. The phrase 'presentation contract' appears three times in the whole repo and zero of the three is code: docs/canon/JPWB-DOC-003:71 (the limb itself), the ratified source at 'Command, Event, Schema Contract Package.md':2466 ('Presentation contracts are separate from semantic contracts'), and enforcement-register.ts:2019 quoting the limb back as RPH-CON-008's canonAnchor.

(2) NO SCHEMA ANYWHERE REFERENCES A COMMAND. This is the stronger half and it is what makes the arm NO_SHAPE rather than BY_CONSTRUCTION. I walked all 128 live schemas (105 command payloads + 23 object schemas) looking for any field whose value space contains a command type, and found ZERO — so 'a contract that references a Command' has no representation in the contract layer in EITHER direction, for presentation contracts or for any other kind. The nearest thing with the word 'contract' in it, DefinePwuType.boundaryContract, resolves to { counterpartyLabel, attestedAssurancePolicyIds, applicabilityNote } — no command reference.

(3) THE RULE IS THEREFORE SATISFIED BY ABSENCE, WHICH IS NOT ENFORCEMENT. I deliberately did NOT score this ENFORCED_BY_CONSTRUCTION. Construction means the forbidden VALUE is unreachable while the SUBJECT exists; here the subject itself is missing, so nothing has been closed against anything — the arrangement is simply unquantifiable. The register reached the identical conclusion in its own vocabulary at RPH-CON-008 and, notably, reached it by ATTEMPT rather than assumption: 'dispatching `UpdateCanvasLayout` carrying a semantic version field, a lifecycle mutation, an assurance disposition and a baseline id returns "Unknown command type", and so does `MoveNode` with an EMPTY payload. A refusal insensitive to the rule's antecedent is not this rule being enforced, and the identical response to both is what closes the ENFORCED arm.' I reproduced that response in my own lane run (UpdateCanvasLayout / MoveNode / ApplyPresentationChange all -> 'Unknown command type'), which is why I am not citing it as an enforcing site for this row.

(4) WHY THIS IS NOT DIVERGENT_UNFILED. There is no divergence to file: nothing enforces the limb and nothing needs to, because no arrangement exists that it would refuse. And the residue IS already recorded — RPH-CON-008 carries this limb's text VERBATIM as its canonAnchor and states the risk in its own voice: 'THE RESIDUE, stated because it is the whole risk: the day a presentation command IS authored, this becomes a live rule with a real subject, and nothing in this register would notice. evidence:
THE LIMB IS A CONJUNCTION AND THE TWO CONJUNCTS COME OUT DIFFERENTLY.

CONJUNCT (a) 'references an active policy version' — ENFORCED, and I drove it. `requestAssuranceAssessment` loads the cited ASSURANCE_POLICY and fails closed twice: once when it does not exist, once when `policy.status !== 'ACTIVE'`. A DRAFT policy is REJECTED with RPH_VALIDATION_SEMANTIC_FAILED; the byte-identical request against the SAME policy after ActivateAssurancePolicy is ACCEPTED. This binds a VERSION and not merely a policy, because a policy version is its own aggregate here: `version` is set once at CreateAssurancePolicy and is absent from EditAssurancePolicyPayloadSchema (messages.ts:712-731), and a successor is a distinct policyId reached via SupersedeAssurancePolicy — so the DRAFT/SUSPENDED/SUPERSEDED status test IS the not-active-version test.

CONJUNCT (b) 'and its subject's exact semantic version' — ADMITTED at BOTH moments, driven. (i) At request: the PWU is at semanticVersion 1 and `subjectSemanticVersions: {pwu: 99}` is ACCEPTED and stored verbatim; `{}` (no version at all for a named subject) is ACCEPTED at request too. (ii) At completion: a validatorResult declaring the subject at v7 while the PWU is at v1 is ACCEPTED, the assessment advances to SATISFIED, and the emitted AssuranceAssessmentCompleted payload records subjectSemanticVersions {pwu: 7} — a SATISFIED verdict in the audit log for a version the subject has never been at.

WHY THE ONE CHECK THAT DOES READ THE FIELD IS NOT THIS. `parseCompletion` (assurance.ts:1818-1830) refuses a completion whose `subjectObjectIds` names a subject with no numeric entry in `subjectSemanticVersions`. That is a COMPLETENESS test (is a version NAMED) and is RPH-ASR-007's ENFORCED limb; it keys on presence, never on equality with the subject. I drove it as the control precisely so the two refusals could be told apart: the SAME command with `{}` is REJECTED at the SAME site while the wrong-number version sails through.

CENSUS OF THE ABSENCE, checked in both directions. Exactly TWO production sites anywhere compare a recorded assessment version against a live subject version, and NEITHER is on the assessment command path: floor-gate.ts:314 (`rec?.version === opts.subjectVersion`) and the pure kernel floor.ts:320 (`r.subjectSemanticVersion === subject.semanticVersion`). evidence:
ENFORCED AT THE FLOOR GATE, ADMITTED ON THE PWU SATISFACTION PLANE. Both halves driven.

ENFORCED HALF. `floorGateBlock` computes `versionOk = rec?.version === opts.subjectVersion`, where `rec.version` is THE SUBJECT VERSION THE RECORDED ASSESSMENT BOUND (latestFloorDispositions reads `s.subjectSemanticVersions?.[subjectId]` off the stored ASSURANCE_ASSESSMENT, floor-gate.ts:245) and `opts.subjectVersion` is THE SUBJECT'S LIVE VERSION READ FROM THE LOADED AGGREGATE (`const version = Number(state.semanticVersion ?? 1);`, pwa-authoring.ts:965). A version-mismatched assessment is downgraded to MISSING and the protected transition is refused. Two live callers: publishPwa via pwaFloorGate (pwa-authoring.ts:966) and completeExecutionStep over each step-output subject (execution.ts:1432).

I RAN THE LANE'S OWN ASR-15:5 TRAP CHECK ON IT — does the predicate read the SUBJECT, or only the payload? It reads the SUBJECT, and I proved it by MOVING the subject rather than forging a number. The floor was recorded SATISFIED at PWA v2; two real authoring commands (DefinePwuType + EditPwuType) then raised the PWA to v4; the identical PublishPwa was REJECTED. The three assessments were byte-identical in probe and control; the only thing that changed was the world. CONTROL: the same drive with the post-floor edit omitted publishes cleanly (ACCEPTED, publicationStatus PUBLISHED), so the refusal discriminates on exactly the relation the limb names and on nothing else.

ADMITTED HALF. `rejectUnbackedDisposition` (pwu.ts:1350-1378) is the guard on ChangePwuState -> assuranceState SATISFIED. It loads each cited object and tests TWO of its fields — `s.assessmentState === p.assuranceState` and `(s.subjectObjectIds ?? []).includes(id)` — and never touches `subjectSemanticVersions`, and never loads the PWU's own semanticVersion. Driven: an assessment REQUESTED and COMPLETED SATISFIED with pin {pwu: 0} — an assessment of version 0 — satisfies a PWU sitting at semanticVersion 1. ACCEPTED, and the PWU's assuranceState really becomes SATISFIED. That is n satisfying n+1, from a true premise, with no forgery anywhere in the arrangement.

SO THE UNION OF THE ENFORCING SITES IS NOT TOTAL, which is why this is not ENFORCED_MULTI_SITE: the version binding is consulted at PWA publication and at execution-step-output completion, and nowhere on the path by which an assessment actually satisfies a work unit.

evidence:
READINESS IS COMPUTED ON READ, NOT STORED, AND I OBSERVED THE RECOMPUTATION CHANGE ITS ANSWER. Two identical worlds differing only in whether InvalidateEvidence was dispatched: in CONTROL, PromoteBaseline => ACCEPTED and baseline.status = AUTHORITATIVE; in TEST, the byte-identical PromoteBaseline => REJECTED / RPH_EVIDENCE_INVALIDATED and the baseline stayed APPROVED. So the invalidation is what moved the answer, and the answer is recomputed at the moment of the deciding read.

THE SITE. `promoteBaseline`'s guard calls `invalidatedEvidenceUnderminingPromotion` (governance.ts:832), which walks FORWARD references off the store — each required assessment's claimIds -> claim.supportingEvidenceIds, plus the promotion decision's consideredEvidenceIds — and returns those whose Evidence.status is INVALIDATED; the refusal at :992 names the evidence AND the claim it reached it through. The same guard also recomputes the rest of readiness from committed state on every dispatch: canPromoteBaseline is handed requiredAssessments (each assessment's current assessmentState, classified by assessmentHasConcluded), openObservations from observationsAgainstBaselineItems, contestedClaims from contestedClaimsAgainstBaselineItems (derived from the store, "not from the promoting payload"), and current subject semanticVersions for decisionAuthorizesVersions. Nothing about readiness is cached.

BY CONSTRUCTION UNDERNEATH IT: BaselineObjectSchema (packages/rph-contracts/src/objects.ts:690) is a z.strictObject whose declared keys are baselineType, purpose, scope, itemObjectVersions, assuranceAssessmentIds, promotionDecisionId, approvalDecisionId, status — no readiness or promotability field anywhere on it, so a stale stored readiness is not merely absent but inexpressible. WHAT THE LIMB FORBIDS: treating model output as anything more trusted than external input.

TWO independent observations, and the second is the discriminating one.

(a) THE PIPELINE IS ORIGIN-BLIND — model-authored commands get the identical treatment. Driving the SAME malformed payload from a HUMAN session and from an AGENT session produced byte-identical refusals (VALIDATION_FAILED / RPH_VALIDATION_SCHEMA_FAILED / 'Schema validation failed'), and byte-identical semantic refusals (CONFLICT / RPH_REVISION_CONFLICT). No trust is extended to model-authored input; none is withheld either. The authoring broker's proposals ARE ordinary commands: packages/rph-authoring/src/broker.ts dispatches every PROPOSE through the engine as an AGENT, and accepting a staged agent turn REPLAYS the recorded commands through dispatchBatchGuarded on the canonical engine (apps/rph-demo/src/lib/server/authoring-turn.ts:463) bound to `getEngine().as(AGENT_CREDENTIAL)` (authoring-turn.ts:227) — never an overlay merge, and never re-attributed to the human who pressed accept.

(b) MODEL OUTPUT IS HELD TO MORE THAN EXTERNAL INPUT, KEYED ON THE OUTPUT'S OWN ORIGIN. The cited site refuses a step completion whose result has not cleared the de minimis floor, where AI-producedness is decided by packages/rph-application/src/handlers/floor-gate.ts:46-47 signal 0 — `prov.executedBy` in AI_ACTOR_TYPES, or `prov.originType` in AI_ORIGIN_TYPES = {MODEL_GENERATION, TOOL_OUTPUT}. I isolated that signal: the ISSUER WAS A HUMAN IN EVERY RUN and only originType varied. USER_INPUT -> ACCEPTED, stepState SUCCEEDED. MODEL_GENERATION -> REJECTED, stepState stays RUNNING. TOOL_OUTPUT -> REJECTED. MIGRATION and IMPORTED -> ACCEPTED (deliberate and documented at floor-gate.ts:33-34: 'MIGRATION / DERIVED / IMPORTED are neither direct-human nor direct-AI'). So the refusal is caused by the OUTPUT'S DECLARED ORIGIN alone, not by who dispatched.

(c) THE MODEL/VALIDATOR OUTPUT BOUNDARY ALSO CLASSIFIES BEFORE ADMITTING. packages/rph-assurance/src/assurance-rules.ts:252-271 classifies a validator result BEFORE it can affect authoritative state: execution failure -> VALIDATOR_FAILED, never REJECTED. THE ENVELOPE IS CLOSED AND SINGLE-SITED. `DomainEventSchema` (packages/rph-contracts/src/envelopes.ts:141-155) is a `z.strictObject` whose complete field set is eventId, eventType, eventSchemaVersion, aggregateType, aggregateId, aggregateRevision, occurredAt, recordedAt, actor, correlationId, causationId?, commandId?, payload. Driven confirmation of that key set over every committed event: `actor, aggregateId, aggregateRevision, aggregateType, commandId, correlationId, eventId, eventSchemaVersion, eventType, occurredAt, payload, recordedAt`. There is NO `rationale` field and NO prior-value field at envelope level, and because the schema is strict there cannot be one. Exactly ONE production site mints an event envelope — `makeEvent`, kit.ts:189-226 — so whatever it does not write cannot appear on any event.

MEASURED LIVE OVER THE SHIPPED REFERENCE UNDERTAKING (332 committed events, 38 distinct event types, driven via `driveReferenceUndertaking`):

  * timestamp .......... occurredAt 332/332 AND recordedAt 332/332. PRESERVED.
  * causal relations ... correlationId 332/332, commandId 332/332. `causationId` is deliberately absent on issued acts and present on derived ones; I RAN verif/causation-provenance.test.ts (3 passed) which asserts both directions. PRESERVED.
  * rationale .......... 10/332 events, on 4 of the 38 driven types only (AssurancePolicyCreated, DecisionEffective, DecisionProposed, DecompositionProposed). Those ten are accidents of the default event payload being `command.payload`; a handler that narrows via the `eventPayload` seam drops it. NOT PRESERVED.
  * prior values ....... 67/332 events, on 2 of the 38 driven types only — PwuStateChanged (66, field `previousState`) and IntentFormalized (1, field `priorSemanticVersion`). Across the ENTIRE ratified message catalog only four payload fields name a prior value at all (messages.ts:252, :830, :1374, :1527). NOT PRESERVED.

THE ONE ARTIFACT THAT DOES HOLD PRIOR VALUES IN FULL IS WRITE-ONLY, and this is the fact that would otherwise dissolve the finding. `professional_work_object_versions` snapshots the entire object state at every revision (sqlite-storage-adapter.ts:197). filing_statement:
WHAT CANON REQUIRES. JPWB-DOC-003 §9 PER-2, limb 1 (canon L341), verbatim: "Every material semantic change produces an immutable domain event preserving prior values, actor, rationale, timestamp, and causal relationships;". FIVE things. Three are preserved by construction; TWO are absent, and the absence cannot be repaired at the envelope without a contract change.

WHAT THE CODE DOES — THE ENVELOPE IS CLOSED AND SINGLE-SITED. `DomainEventSchema` (packages/rph-contracts/src/envelopes.ts:141-155) is a `z.strictObject` whose complete field set is eventId, eventType, eventSchemaVersion, aggregateType, aggregateId, aggregateRevision, occurredAt, recordedAt, actor, correlationId, causationId?, commandId?, payload. There is NO `rationale` field and NO prior-value field at envelope level, and because the schema is STRICT there cannot be one. Exactly ONE production site mints an envelope — `makeEvent`, packages/rph-application/src/handlers/kit.ts:189-226 (the actor stamp at :209) — so whatever it does not write cannot appear on any event. I verified there is no second builder: `eventId:` in production non-test code across packages/ + apps/ resolves to that one mint plus the zod declaration; the other hits are CSAA's unrelated graph type.

MEASURED LIVE OVER THE SHIPPED REFERENCE UNDERTAKING (332 committed events, 38 distinct event types, driven via `driveReferenceUndertaking`; re-run this pass):
  * actor .............. 332/332 (event types missing actor: none). PRESERVED.
  * timestamp .......... occurredAt 332/332 AND recordedAt 332/332. PRESERVED.
  * causal relations ... correlationId 332/332, commandId 332/332; `causationId` deliberately absent on issued acts and present on derived ones, asserted both directions by verif/causation-provenance.test.ts (3 passed). PRESERVED.
  * rationale .......... 10/332 events, on 4 of the 38 driven types only (AssurancePolicyCreated, DecisionEffective, DecisionProposed, DecompositionProposed). Those ten are ACCIDENTS of the default event payload being `command.payload`; any handler that narrows via the `eventPayload` seam silently drops it. NOT PRESERVED.
  * prior values ....... 67/332 events, on 2 of the 38 driven types only — PwuStateChanged (66, field `previousState`) and IntentFormalized (1, field `priorSemanticVersion`). Across the ENTIRE ratified message catalog only four payload fields name a prior value at all (messages.ts:252, :830, :1374, :1527). NOT PRESERVED.
DUMPED VERBATIM, so this is not an inference from field names: `PwuShapingStarted -> {"workLifecycleState":"SHAPING"}` — the value it replaced, PROPOSED, appears nowhere in the event. `ExecutionPlanApproved -> {"status":"APPROVED"}`. `ExecutionStepStarted -> {"stepId":"stp_…","stepState":"RUNNING"}`. `BaselinePromoted -> {…,"status":"AUTHORITATIVE"}`. Each records the new value and not the old.

⚠ THE FINDING MUST RECORD BOTH HALVES, BECAUSE THE SECOND IS WHAT WOULD OTHERWISE DISSOLVE IT. `professional_work_object_versions` snapshots the entire object state at every revision (packages/rph-persistence/src/sqlite-storage-adapter.ts:197). A repo-wide census of that table name returns EXACTLY TWO hits — its CREATE TABLE (packages/rph-persistence/src/schema.ts:81) and that one INSERT — and ZERO SELECTs. The `StorageAdapter` port declares no version-history reader (its nine methods are getReceipt, loadObject, commit, transaction, readAggregateEvents, readAllEvents, readPendingOutbox, markOutboxPublished, close). So prior values ARE persisted — into a table no code path in the repository can read. Not "preserved by a different mechanism": preserved nowhere reachable. A reader who discovers that table will otherwise conclude the obligation is discharged.

⚠ HALF-RECORDED ALREADY — CITE, DO NOT RE-FILE. docs/_working/BACKLOG.md item (8), "Write-only fields (the REG-F-005 shape, alive) — RE-VERIFIED 2026-08-20 with identifier-boundary searches", names `professional_work_object_versions` as one of three confirmed write-only carriers — "(CREATE at `schema.ts:81`, one INSERT at `sqlite-storage-adapter.ts:197`, zero SELECTs). Those three are the REG-F-005 shape and are sweep-or-file." That records the WRITE-ONLY fact under a storage-hygiene heading. It does NOT connect it to PER-2, and it says nothing about the domain event omitting prior values or rationale — which is the primary half and the reason this table's unreadability matters.

NOTHING RECORDS THE PRIMARY HALF. REG-005 mentions PER-2 exactly ZERO times as a subject (the one string hit at :1368 is a citation-correction list). The two enforcement-register rows citing PER-2 are RPH-PER rows on OTHER clauses (:2359 append-only / materialized-state subordination; :2462 the upcaster obligation). The guard-enforcement ledger has no PER-2 row. No docblock states that events omit prior values or rationale. The NEAREST artifact is verif/causation-provenance.test.ts, whose header QUOTES this exact five-item list — "PER-2 adds that every material semantic change produces an event 'preserving prior values, actor, rationale, timestamp, and CAUSAL RELATIONSHIPS'" — and then covers ONLY causation, resting explicitly on PER-9 rather than PER-2. A file that quotes the five and tests one is the clearest evidence that the other four were never adjudicated.

THE REMEDY, AND IT IS A CONTRACT CHANGE, NOT A WIRE. (a) RATIONALE: decide whether canon's "rationale" is an envelope obligation or a per-event-payload one, and say so. If envelope: `DomainEventSchema` is `z.strictObject`, so it must gain the field and `makeEvent` must stamp it from the command — today's 10/332 is an accident of payload pass-through and will vanish the next time a handler narrows via `eventPayload`. If payload: the ratified message catalog must declare it on every material-change event, and the entry should say which. (b) PRIOR VALUES: either declare a prior-value field on each material-change event payload (four exist today out of 38 driven types), or give the `StorageAdapter` port a version-history reader and a read surface that uses it, so the table that already holds every prior state stops being write-only. Either way the entry must state both halves together; closing one alone leaves the invariant unmet and looks closed.

evidence:
THE LIMB HAS TWO READINGS AND THEY DIVERGE — the sequence half holds completely, the state half is bounded and the bound is filed.

HISTORY-AS-SEQUENCE HOLDS, MEASURED NOT ASSUMED. Over the driven Reference Undertaking (332 events across 88 aggregates), 88/88 aggregate streams are gapless, strictly ordered and start at revision 0 — zero exceptions. The read at the cited line is `SELECT payload FROM domain_events WHERE aggregate_type=? AND aggregate_id=? ORDER BY aggregate_revision ASC`, and the `payload` column holds `JSON.stringify(e)` — the WHOLE event, not just its payload (sqlite-storage-adapter.ts:202-216) — so nothing of the envelope is lost on the round trip. Gaplessness is structural rather than checked: `commitState` derives `newRevision` as `loaded.revision + 1` and hands the event the same number, so no command can choose a revision (this is RPH-PER-005's census, which I re-verified: `ctx.store.commit` has exactly one production caller).

HISTORY-AS-STATE IS BOUNDED, AND THE BOUND IS LARGE. The drive produces 15 aggregate types: ASSURANCE_ASSESSMENT:136, PROFESSIONAL_WORK_UNIT:98, EXECUTION_PLAN:40, EVIDENCE:16, CLAIM:9, BASELINE:8, ASSURANCE_POLICY:5, INTENT:5, DECISION:4, DECOMPOSITION_CONTRACT:4, OBLIGATION:3, ARTIFACT:1, ASSUMPTION:1, ASSURANCE_OBSERVATION:1, CONSTRAINT:1. Exactly ONE of the fifteen has a reducer that reconstructs the object from its own stream — `replayPwuAxes` (packages/rph-projections/src/pwu-replay.ts:49). I drove it: 13/13 PWUs rebuild and match the materialized object, 0 mismatches. But it restores FOUR of the materialized PWU object's THIRTY-FOUR fields. Nothing reconstructs an Intent, a Decision, a Baseline, an ExecutionPlan or an AssuranceAssessment — the last being the most event-dense aggregate in the drive at 136 events.

AND LIMB 1'S GAP COMPOUNDS HERE. Because 265 of 332 events carry only the NEW value, folding a stream yields the END state rather than the succession of values that 'how it became authoritative' names; and `professional_work_object_versions`, which does hold that succession, has zero readers.

THE DIVERGENCE IS RECORDED. RPH-PER-006's `why` states both bounds in its own words, and it names them as limits rather than as coverage — which is why this is PARTIAL_DIVERGENT_FILED and not DIVERGENT_UNFILED.

evidence:
THE ARRANGEMENT IS INEXPRESSIBLE BECAUSE THE FIELD THAT WOULD HAVE TO BE ABSENT DOES NOT EXIST.

`CommitArgs.event` is declared `readonly event: DomainEvent;` — REQUIRED, not optional (kit.ts:252). `commitState` is the ONLY production constructor of a `CommitInput`: the census of `CommitInput` over non-test production files returns ten references, of which exactly one is a construction (kit.ts:503 `const input: CommitInput = {`) and the rest are the port declaration (storage.ts:43, :75), the two adapters' method signatures, three imports and two comments. That single construction sets `events: [args.event, ...(args.alsoEvents ?? [])]`, whose length is therefore always >= 1. And `ctx.store.commit` has exactly ONE production caller, kit.ts:529. So the chain from 'materialized state moves' to 'at least one event is appended' has no branch in it.

A SECOND, INDEPENDENT LIMB AT THE CONTRACT LAYER. All 105 entries in the ratified COMMANDS registry declare `emitsEvent` (driven: `missing emitsEvent = 0 []`), and packages/csaa/src/graph/build-command-event-contract-overlay.ts:1143 throws `COMMANDS.<name>.emitsEvent is absent.` — so a command with no declared event cannot even be registered. The two limbs are independent: one could hold while the other broke.

ON THE WORD 'READ MODELS', BOTH READINGS LAND IN THE SAME PLACE, so I did not have to choose one. Under the PROJECTION reading the limb is vacuously satisfied: the schema declares five tables and none is a read model, `IncrementalProjection`'s checkpoint is an in-process integer, and the demo surfaces re-fold the whole event log per request (this is RPH-PER-009/011's census, which I re-verified against schema.ts). There is no persisted projection for a handler to update. Under the MATERIALIZED-CURRENT-STATE reading — the normalized `professional_work_objects` row, which is what §9's opening paragraph calls the read side — it is satisfied by the construction above.

DRIVEN CONTROL IN BOTH DIRECTIONS, because a construction claim with no control discriminates nothing. ACCEPTED commands move state AND history together (CaptureIntent: events 0->1, INTENT revision 0; ProposePwu: events 1->2, PWU revision 0). A REFUSED command moves NEITHER (ChangePwuState PROPOSED->EXECUTING: events 2->2, delta 0; revision 0->0; workLifecycleState PROPOSED->PROPOSED).

THE WEAKNESS, STATED RATHER THAN HIDDEN (see census_gated=false): nothing committed would redden if `event` were made optional or a second commit caller were added. verif/emitted-event-guard.ts wraps `commit` on both shipped adapters, but it only validates event PAYLOAD shapes and skips events without a commandId — a zero-event commit would pass through it silently.

The decisive test is whether the engine can DISTINGUISH a caller that reloaded current state and re-formed intent from one that took the refusal's number and bumped it. I drove both, in one process, against identical aggregates. FORBIDDEN ARRANGEMENT: caller A read the INTENT at revision 0 (RAW) and formed the payload object `{ambiguityIds: []}` against that read; a concurrent writer ran BeginIntentDiscovery -> revision 1 (UNDER_DISCOVERY); caller A dispatched ProvisionIntent at expectedRevision=0 and was correctly refused with RPH_REVISION_CONFLICT; caller A then resubmitted THE SAME payload object — never reloading, never re-reading state, never re-deciding — with expectedRevision bumped to believed+1. ALSO ACCEPTED. THE TWO RUNS PRODUCE BYTE-IDENTICAL AGGREGATE STREAMS — [0,1,2] and [0,1,2], same event types, same revisions, same final PROVISIONAL state. There is nothing in the record that differs, which is what "no shape" means concretely: the engine did not fail to check, it has nothing to check against. WHY THIS IS NOT UNENFORCED_DEAD_PREDICATE: a dead predicate needs a predicate. There is no branch anywhere that reads read-provenance, because no field carries it. The command envelope (packages/rph-contracts/src/envelopes.ts:100+, `domainCommandSchema`) is commandId / commandType / commandSchemaVersion / targetAggregateType / targetAggregateId / expectedRevision / issuedAt / issuedBy? / correlationId / causationId? / idempotencyKey / payload. `expectedRevision` records a NUMBER the caller asserts; nothing records the STATE the caller saw, when it saw it, or that it looked again after being refused. BOTH HALVES, AND THEY DISAGREE. Scripts: scratchpad/lane-PER-6c.mjs, lane-PER-6d.mjs, lane-PER-6e.mjs.

HALF ONE — THE ENGINE SEAM SATISFIES THE LIMB, AND I DROVE IT RATHER THAN ASSUMING IT. I built a second Engine over the same store (process restart, database survives) and confirmed that professional decisions are re-derived from durable rows, not carried in process memory: (a) the RPH-EXE-008 retry cap refused the third attempt AFTER the restart, and it can only have counted by folding ExecutionStepStarted events out of the store (`attemptsMadeFrom(ctx.store.readAllEvents(), ...)`); (b) an idempotency key first used before the restart returned status DUPLICATE with no new event from a brand-new Engine, so the receipt is a `command_receipts` row and not a Map; (c) the §36.2 failure-class refusal reads `ctx.store.readAggregateEvents(...)`. Handlers receive `ctx.store` and nothing process-scoped. Census of module-level mutable containers in the decision path (packages/rph-application/src, rph-domain/src, rph-engine/src, rph-persistence/src, tests excluded) returns 14 bindings and every one is a frozen constant vocabulary — ReadonlySet/Set of enum members (FLOOR_POLICY_ID_SET, ESCALATABLE_SEVERITIES, LIVE_CONSTRAINT_STATUSES, AI_STEP_TYPES, BLOCKING_SEVERITIES, PROMOTABLE_DISPOSITIONS, ...) — never written after initialisation. No cache, no session map, no memo.

HALF TWO — AND IT IS WHY THIS ROW IS NOT A CERTIFICATION. In the shipped host, a professionally material binding lives ONLY in process memory and has NO durable field to live in. apps/rph-demo/src/lib/server/workbench.ts:52 declares `const undertakingIntent = new Map<string, string>();` with the comment "Bridge: a fresh Undertaking's originating Intent id, remembered until its first PWU exists". It is written by the create-Undertaking route action (apps/rph-demo/src/routes/undertakings/+page.server.ts:127, `registerUndertakingIntent(undertakingId, intentId)`) and read by `resolveIntentId` (apps/rph-demo/src/routes/undertakings/[id]/+page.server.ts:498-505), whose result decides whether the Undertaking's FIRST PWU can be created at all — [id]/+page.server.ts:692-694 bails with 'This Undertaking has no originating intent to bind the PWU to.' when it is absent.

I PROVED THE BINDING IS INEXPRESSIBLE DURABLY BY DRIVING IT, WITH A CONTROL. `CreateUndertaking` carrying an `intentId` is refused by the contract itself — CreateUndertakingPayloadSchema (packages/rph-contracts/src/messages.ts:643) is a `z.strictObject` of eight fields with no intent among them — and the SAME command with only that field removed passes schema validation and reaches SEMANTIC validation instead, failing on an unrelated missing PWA. Two different error codes from one field: RPH_VALIDATION_SCHEMA_FAILED vs RPH_VALIDATION_SEMANTIC_FAILED. So the rejection is caused by `intentId` specifically, not by the payload generally. The ratified object schema agrees: packages/rph-contracts/schemas/objects/Undertaking.json declares 24 properties and not one is intent-bearing, while `intentId` appears in exactly ONE ratified object schema repo-wide, ProfessionalWorkUnit.json — which is precisely the host's fallback story ('resolvable from any of the Undertaking's PWUs') and precisely why the gap is real when no PWU exists yet.

WHY THIS IS THIS LIMB AND NOT ANOTHER. Canon's own register applies the same sentence to exactly this shape: RPH-PER-013 carries canonAnchor 'Professional correctness never depends on in-memory state' and reads the property as SURVIVAL — 'the pending decision remains available' across a restart — and certifies it there because 'the Decision is a row in the durable store'. By that standard an Undertaking whose originating Intent is unavailable after a restart is a violation of exactly the property the register certifies elsewhere. It fails CLOSED, which is the good half and I say so: no incorrect record is producible, only an Undertaking permanently unable to acquire its first PWU. But the affordance to establish the trace-spine link depends on which process is running, and that is what the limb forbids.

WHY NOT ENFORCED_BY_CONSTRUCTION. Certifying this limb would assert that no professionally material state lives in process memory. One does, in production server code, with no field to hold it. Burying that in `owed` under a green verdict is what this audit's DIVERGENT_UNFILED arm exists to prevent.

CENSUS RESULT: IMPACTS 0/0/0, REALIZES 0/0/0, DEFINES 0/0/0 across enums.ts, traceability.ts and traceability-view.ts, against a control that returned non-zero in 10 of 12 cells over the same three files with the same pattern. The 17-member registry, printed at runtime, contains none of the three.

THE THREE CONCEPTS, CHECKED ONE AT A TIME FOR A DIFFERENTLY-SPELLED CARRIER (limb 11 makes spelling free, so absence of the token is not yet absence of the meaning):
  • REALIZATION — CARRIED, but only in the projection and under another name. packages/rph-projections/src/traceability-view.ts:14 declares `| 'TRACES_TO_INTENT' // PWU -> the intent it realizes`. The comment uses the family's own verb. I drove it: after CaptureIntent + ProposePwu the live projection held `{"from":PWU,"to":INTENT,"type":"TRACES_TO_INTENT"}`. So realization is the ONE member of this family that exists anywhere in running code — and it exists in the nine-member ad-hoc projection vocabulary, not in the ratified 17.
  • DEFINITION (type binding) — ABSENT EVERYWHERE. The source spine names it: docs/canon/_extracts/extract-doc003-a.md:41 quotes RPH-DOC-003 L291-331 as 'Intent DEFINES Desired Outcome'. And the type-binding relation the engine most needs — PWU instance to PWU Type — is carried as a FIELD (`pwuTypeId`, read at packages/rph-projections/src/execution-view.ts:995-1035) with no edge token: `grep -rn "INSTANCE_OF|'DEFINES'|TYPE_OF" packages apps` (non-dist, non-CSAA) returned zero.
  • IMPACT — ABSENT AS A RELATION, and the surrounding machinery is dead. IMPACT_CLASSIFICATIONS (packages/rph-domain/src/traceability.ts:7) is a seven-value NODE classification, not an edge type, and `impactedObjects` computes impact by REACHABILITY over other relations rather than by an IMPACTS edge. The register states it has no production caller (RPH-INT-006, re-confirmed under REG-F-199), and packages/rph-application/src/handlers/decomposition.ts:441 says so inside a rejection string: 'impact analysis ... this engine has no impact-analysis plane (impactedObjects has no caller and needs a TraceLink-minting surface)'.

SO: 0 of 3 in the registry, 1 of 3 (realization) alive at the projection layer under a repository spelling, 2 of 3 (impact, definition) with no carrier of any spelling anywhere.
