REG-F-<next> - The ratified 17-value `TraceRelation` set omits relation concepts REL-1 names as required semantic families; family 9 (impact, realization, definition) is the only family in limbs 2-9 with NO member at all.

⚠ ONE ENTRY, FOUR LIMBS. This finding is shared with limb:REL-1:8 and, in its general form, is the same entry limbs REL-1:6 and REL-1:7 already ask for. The filing pass must write ONE entry, not four: a single change to `TraceRelationSchema` closes all of them.

WHAT CANON REQUIRES. JPWB-DOC-003 §5 REL-1 (heading at line 151, statement at line 153), limb 9: "impact, realization, and definition (consequence and type binding)." The general form, DERIVED rather than enumerated: the Coding Agent Guide §5.5 stable-core grid (L429-435), which DOC-003's provenance sidecar line 35 names as REL-1's source, lists 23 tokens; `packages/rph-contracts/src/enums.ts:745-763` ratifies 17; the six omitted are IMPLEMENTS, VALIDATES, APPROVES, IMPACTS, REALIZES, DEFINES.

THIS LIMB'S SHARE, AND THE ENTRY MUST RECORD THE ASYMMETRY. Family 9 names THREE concepts and the ratified registry carries ZERO. Every other family in limbs 2-9 carries at least one member.

WHAT THE CODE DOES. Driven (node, real contracts):
  RATIFIED SET (17) = [DERIVED_FROM, REFINES, DECOMPOSES, SATISFIES, DEPENDS_ON, CONSTRAINED_BY, ASSUMES, PRODUCES, SUPPORTS, CONTRADICTS, VERIFIES, INVALIDATES, SUPERSEDES, PROMOTES, ALLOCATES, PROPAGATES, GOVERNS]
  TraceRelationSchema.parse('IMPACTS') -> REFUSED ; parse('REALIZES') -> REFUSED ; parse('DEFINES') -> REFUSED
  TraceLinkSchema.safeParse({...relation:'IMPACTS'}) -> REFUSED, exactly ONE issue, path ["relation"]; identically for 'REALIZES' and 'DEFINES'
  CONTROL, the identical fixture with ONLY `relation` changed: 'PROMOTES', 'GOVERNS', 'SUPERSEDES', 'DECOMPOSES' -> ACCEPTED (4 of 4)
SITES: `packages/rph-contracts/src/enums.ts:745-763` (the ratified set); `packages/rph-domain/src/traceability.ts` `TRACE_DIRECTIONALITY` (no row for any of the three).

EACH CONCEPT CHECKED FOR A DIFFERENTLY-SPELLED CARRIER, because REL-1 limb 11 makes spelling free, so a missing token is not yet a missing meaning.
  REALIZATION is carried ONLY in the projection's ad-hoc vocabulary: `packages/rph-projections/src/traceability-view.ts:14` declares `| 'TRACES_TO_INTENT' // PWU -> the intent it realizes`, using the family's own verb - and TRACES_TO_INTENT appears in NO ratified registry.
  DEFINITION (type binding) has no carrier of any spelling. The type-binding relation the engine most needs - PWU instance to PWU type - is a FIELD, `pwuTypeId`, read at `packages/rph-projections/src/execution-view.ts:995` (`if (!inst.pwuTypeId) return { reason: 'no-type' };`). Census: `grep -rn "INSTANCE_OF\|'DEFINES'\|TYPE_OF" --include=*.ts packages apps | grep -v /dist/ | grep -v csaa` -> 0 hits, against a CONTROL of 152 references to `permittedChildTypeIds` over the identical population. The type machinery is enormous and fully present; it simply never expresses type binding as a relation.
  IMPACT has no relation carrier and its surrounding machinery is dead. `IMPACT_CLASSIFICATIONS` (packages/rph-domain/src/traceability.ts:7) is a seven-value NODE classification, not an edge type. `impactedObjects` computes impact by REACHABILITY over other relations and has no production caller - `packages/rph-application/src/handlers/decomposition.ts:441` says so inside a rejection string: "this engine has no impact-analysis plane (impactedObjects has no caller and needs a TraceLink-minting surface)".

THE INTERLOCK, WHICH BELONGS IN THE ENTRY BECAUSE IT SHOWS THE ABSENCE IS NOT MERELY COSMETIC. The kernel graph ACCEPTS the very tokens the contract refuses: `TraceGraph.addLink` with `relation:'IMPACTS'`, `'REALIZES'`, `'DEFINES'` and even `''` (DECISION->BASELINE) are all ACCEPTED, while the CONTROL `addLink 'PROMOTES' BASELINE->DECISION` is REFUSED with "Invalid trace link: PROMOTES source must be one of DECISION, got BASELINE". So the type-level and object-level surfaces disagree about the vocabulary, in the direction that lets an unregistered relation into the kernel graph while barring it from the ratified object.

THE ENTRY MUST ALSO RECORD, because it is the same defect one layer down and no filing names it: the traceability projection has minted a PARALLEL nine-member vocabulary (`packages/rph-projections/src/traceability-view.ts:12-21` - DECOMPOSES, TRACES_TO_INTENT, CHILD_OF, ASSESSES, ABOUT, SUPPORTS, OBLIGATION_OF, AFFECTS, BASELINES) of which SEVEN appear in no ratified registry. That is limbs REL-1:11/12's filing; cross-reference it here rather than duplicate it.

⚠ NOT AN AMENDMENT TO `packages/rph-contracts/vocab/canonical-vocabulary.json:2659-2663`. That divergence block names DEFINES and REALIZED_BY only as DOC-006 FIXTURE display labels it is DISMISSING ("resolved as display-only, non-authoritative"), records no gap against REL-1, and its resolution runs the other way; IMPACTS is not in it at all. It is the wrong home and would read as a duplicate closure.

REMEDY. Mint IMPACTS / REALIZES / DEFINES into `TraceRelationSchema` under the divergence protocol, with `TRACE_DIRECTIONALITY` rows for each, OR amend REL-1's family-9 gloss to drop the three concepts. Because the token set is canon-governed, the entry should state which of the two it is choosing rather than leave the choice to the implementer. Red-first: `TraceLinkSchema.safeParse({...relation:'IMPACTS'})` must ACCEPT while a genuinely unregistered token still refuses, and `TraceGraph.addLink` must stop admitting `''`.

filing_statement:
WHAT CANON REQUIRES. JPWB-DOC-003 §8 ASR-15, line 308, limb 2: "no effective governance decision exists until an authorized actor decides."

WHAT THE CODE DOES. `ApproveDecision` and `GrantWaiver` reach EFFECTIVE through the shared `guard` inside `makeDecisionEffective`, whose predicate is packages/rph-application/src/handlers/governance.ts:332 — `const authorityHeld = authority?.actorType === 'HUMAN';` — computed from the DECISION's RECORDED `authority`, and never from `command.issuedBy`. `ApproveDecisionPayloadSchema` (packages/rph-contracts/src/messages.ts:229-235) has no `authority` key at all, so the actor issuing the approving command declares nothing and is asked nothing. And the act is not a bare lever-pull: `approveDecision`'s `extraMutate` (governance.ts:425-448) OVERWRITES `selectedOption`, `rationale`, `consideredEvidenceIds` and `consideredObservationIds` from the APPROVE payload.

THE DRIVEN ARRANGEMENT (through Engine.dispatch; the anchors re-verified at HEAD 689440d7). A HUMAN proposes honestly: `ProposeDecision` issuedBy HUMAN u1, selectedOption "REJECT-the-change", rationale "human said no" -> ACCEPTED; PROPOSED state reads selectedOption "REJECT-the-change" / rationale "human said no". Then `ApproveDecision` issuedBy AGENT agent-1, selectedOption "SHIP-IT", rationale "agent said yes" -> ACCEPTED. EFFECTIVE state: status EFFECTIVE | selectedOption "SHIP-IT" | rationale "agent said yes" | authority {"actorId":"u1","actorType":"HUMAN","displayName":"Operator"}. The `DecisionEffective` event — the audit fact — carries {"selectedOption":"SHIP-IT","rationale":"agent said yes", …}, and the event actor stamps read [{DecisionProposed, HUMAN u1}, {DecisionEffective, AGENT agent-1}]. An effective governance decision now exists whose CONTENT no authorized actor ever decided, recorded under a human's authority.
CONTROLS, all observed in the same run, proving the site discriminates rather than admitting everything: (A1) ProposeDecision issuedBy AGENT with authority=AGENT -> ACCEPTED PROPOSED, then ApproveDecision issuedBy AGENT -> UNAUTHORIZED | RPH_AUTHORITY_INSUFFICIENT | "Decision dec_… cannot become effective: actor lacks sufficient authority to make this decision effective", state left PROPOSED, revision 0, events ["DecisionProposed"]. (A2) The honest HUMAN path -> ACCEPTED, EFFECTIVE, revision 1. (A4) BIRTH: ProposeDecision with `status:"EFFECTIVE"` in the payload -> VALIDATION_FAILED | RPH_VALIDATION_SCHEMA_FAILED, object ABSENT. So the two shapes the limb most obviously names ARE refused; the third is admitted.
THE ASYMMETRY IS DECIDED THE OTHER WAY ONE HANDLER DOWN, which is what makes this a missing limb rather than a design: `revokeDecision`'s guard (governance.ts:490) reads `command.issuedBy.actorType === 'HUMAN'` and its comment says why — "THE ISSUER, not the decision's recorded authority — because the question this asks is whether THIS ACTOR may withdraw". Driven on the same aggregate in the same run: RevokeDecision issuedBy AGENT -> UNAUTHORIZED, while ApproveDecision issuedBy AGENT -> ACCEPTED. Approval asks the opposite question of the opposite field.

THE LIMB HAS TWO CLAUSES AND THE ENGINE SATISFIES THE SECOND ONLY BECAUSE THE FIRST IS VACUOUS.

CLAUSE A — 'Risk proportionality governs assurance'. The ONLY production predicate anywhere that reads a risk LEVEL is the RISK_AT_LEAST op of the DOC-007 §18 ApplicabilityExpression grammar (packages/rph-assurance/src/applicability.ts:71-78). It resolves `$.riskProfile` off the subject it is handed and compares the level index. It has exactly TWO production call sites, and BOTH hand it a subject projection from which riskProfile has been dropped:

So `resolvePath(subject,'$.riskProfile')` is `undefined` on every dispatch, applicability.ts:73 returns false, and the comparison at :77 (`actualIdx >= requiredIdx`) is UNREACHABLE. The predicate is stuck FALSE regardless of what any command puts on the wire.

PROVEN BY DRIVE, NOT ASSERTED. I created three ACTIVE above-floor policies differing only in their applicability expression, and two PWUs at the extremes of the ratified ladder — HI = {consequence CRITICAL, uncertainty CRITICAL, irreversibility CRITICAL, securitySensitivity HIGH, regulatoryExposure HIGH}, LO = {LOW, LOW, LOW, NONE, NONE}, both read back off the store to confirm they persisted. A policy scoped `RISK_AT_LEAST(CONSEQUENCE, LOW)` — the WEAKEST condition the ladder can express, satisfied by every legal value except NONE — was refused NOT_APPLICABLE against the CRITICAL-consequence PWU. TWO CONTROLS on the same channel published the discrimination: the same policy with NO expression was ACCEPTED, and the same policy with a non-risk expression (`EXISTS $.objectType`) was ACCEPTED. So the expression channel is live and CAN return true; it is the RISK dimension specifically that cannot.

CLAUSE B — 'above a mandatory floor'. It holds, and it holds VACUOUSLY. floorGateBlock's option object is `{aiProduced, subjectVersion, now}` (floor-gate.ts:305-309); FLOOR_POLICY_IDS_REQUIRED is a const array (floor-gate.ts:20-24); deMinimisFloorPlan takes an AssuranceSubject (rph-assurance/src/floor.ts:27-35) which has no risk field. evidence:
THE LIMB IS A SEQUENCE CLAIM WITH A PERMISSION AND AN OBLIGATION, AND BOTH HALVES ARE OBSERVABLE.

THE PERMISSION ('Deterministic failure may short-circuit an obviously invalid candidate'). Driven as PART A. An AGENT-created PWA (createdBy.actorType = AGENT, read back off the store, so `aiProduced` is true at pwaFloorGate) was carried to VALIDATED with floor.schema-invariant recorded REJECTED and floor.identity-provenance SATISFIED at its current version, and NO Reasoning Review ever requested. PublishPwa was refused naming the deterministic failure FIRST: '(floor.schema-invariant=REJECTED, floor.reasoning-review=MISSING)'. The engine never demands that a Reasoning Review be RUN before refusing a candidate that already fails step 1 — the short-circuit is available and costs nothing. floorGateBlock does not literally short-circuit (it maps all three required policies and filters), but it never requires the review to have been performed, which is what the permission grants.

THE OBLIGATION ('but its repaired successor must still receive Reasoning Review before admission'). Driven as PART B, and arranged to make carry-over maximally tempting rather than trivially absent. The candidate at v2 carried floor.schema-invariant=REJECTED (the deterministic failure), floor.identity-provenance=SATISFIED, AND a genuinely performed floor.reasoning-review=SATISFIED at v2. It was then REPAIRED — a second PWU Type defined and the root's child list edited, each of which materially edits the graph and raises the PWA's semanticVersion (pwa-authoring.ts:481, :733) — landing the repaired successor at v4. Both deterministic policies were re-run and recorded SATISFIED at v4 with a strictly later timestamp, so they win the 'latest by updatedAt' selection at floor-gate.ts:242. The ONLY thing not re-run at v4 was the Reasoning Review.

RESULT: PublishPwa REJECTED on EXACTLY ONE conjunct — '(floor.reasoning-review=MISSING)' — with publicationStatus still VALIDATED. A SINGLE-CONJUNCT refusal, so the arrangement does not trip two guards and prove neither. And the word MISSING is produced by the version pin, not by absence: a SATISFIED floor.reasoning-review record for this exact subject EXISTS in the store; floor-gate.ts:314 computes versionOk = (rec.version === 2) === (subjectVersion === 4) => false, and :317 then reports the disposition as 'MISSING'. Neutralise that one line and rec.disposition is 'SATISFIED', the filter at :321 drops it, floorGateBlock returns null, and the repaired successor publishes with a review of its predecessor. That is precisely the arrangement the limb forbids.

THE CONTROL — the nearest-neighbour arrangement that MUST be admitted. Identical state, one command added: a floor.reasoning-review recorded SATISFIED at v4. PublishPwa -> ACCEPTED, publicationStatus PUBLISHED. So the gate is not blanket-refusing an AI-produced PWA; it is refusing the specific arrangement 'repaired successor whose review belongs to the predecessor', and admitting the specific arrangement 'repaired successor reviewed at its own version'.

WHY THE 'REPAIRED SUCCESSOR' IS A NEW VERSION AND NOT A NEW OBJECT. The execution-plane form of the same claim is weaker but concordant: an artifact repaired into a NEW object id has no floor record at all, so stepResultSubjects/floorGateBlock refuse it for plain MISSING. I drove the version form because it is the one a carry-over could defeat, and because it is the one the site actually discriminates.

WHAT CANON REQUIRES. JPWB-DOC-003 §8.2 ASR-3, line 249, limb 5: "Deterministic failure may short-circuit an obviously invalid candidate, but its repaired successor must still receive Reasoning Review before admission." Reinforced by that same line's closing sentence ("A missing, STALE, malformed, failed, unavailable, or independence-invalid required review cannot satisfy assurance or permit its protected transition") and by line 251's SCOPE ("material by default when it creates or changes professional content").

WHAT THE CODE DOES. The de minimis floor gate binds a satisfied assessment to the subject's semanticVersion at packages/rph-application/src/handlers/floor-gate.ts:314 — `const versionOk = opts.subjectVersion === undefined || rec?.version === opts.subjectVersion;` — a real check. The PWA authoring surface splits in two on whether it moves that version. DefinePwuType (pwa-authoring.ts:481), EditPwuType (:733) and RemovePwuType (:817) route through `withPwaVersionBump` / `bumpPwaSemanticVersion`, whose `const newSemanticVersion = loaded.semanticVersion + 1;` is at :178. `editPwa` (declared pwa-authoring.ts:503) commits `newSemanticVersion: loaded.semanticVersion` at :538 — NO bump — while writing `name`, `description`, `domain` and `version` from the payload. A METADATA repair therefore changes the reviewed subject materially without moving the version the floor binds, and the version pin cannot see it. The gate's refusal surface is pwa-authoring.ts:980 (`pwaFloorGate`, declared :959).

THE DRIVEN ARRANGEMENT (through Engine.dispatch, node; both anchor lines re-verified byte-identical at HEAD 689440d7). An AGENT-created PWA (createdBy.actorType read back = AGENT) at semanticVersion 2, floor recorded at v2 as floor.schema-invariant=REJECTED — the deterministic short-circuit the limb expressly permits — floor.identity-provenance=SATISFIED, and a genuinely performed floor.reasoning-review=SATISFIED over the v1.0.0 content. REPAIR: `EditPwa { version: '2.0.0', description: 'the REPAIRED v2.0.0 text, which no reviewer has read' }` -> ACCEPTED; the declared version moves 1.0.0 -> 2.0.0, the description is materially different, semanticVersion stays 2. Then SubmitPwaForReview, ValidatePwa, PublishPwa -> ACCEPTED, publicationStatus PUBLISHED. The PWA is published as 2.0.0 carrying a Reasoning Review performed on the 1.0.0 text: the limb's forbidden arrangement, literally.
CONTROL-REFUSE, and it is what makes this a defect rather than a reading. The byte-identical arrangement repaired through the GRAPH channel instead (DefinePwuType + EditPwuType on the root; semanticVersion 2 -> 4) is refused at the same gate on exactly ONE conjunct: REJECTED | RPH_INVARIANT_VIOLATION | "PublishPwa blocked: the de minimis assurance floor is not SATISFIED for PWA pwa_00000000000000000000000001 at v4 (floor.reasoning-review=MISSING). …", publicationStatus left VALIDATED. CONTROL-ACCEPT: that same graph repair with the review re-run at v4 -> ACCEPTED, PUBLISHED. So the gate discriminates precisely the sequence this limb states, and the metadata channel walks around it.

WHY NOTHING RECORDS IT, AND WHAT THE RECORD SAYS INSTEAD. docs/_working/HARMONIZATION-FINDINGS.md:28 (finding #18) filed the GENERAL claim — "The PWA's semanticVersion is never bumped by any authoring command, so the floor gate's version binding is inert" — and the remediation reached the graph channel only. pwa-authoring.ts:125-146's WHY comment names the exact hazard and then scopes itself to the three PWU-Type commands without disclosing the omission; editPwa's own docblock (:498-501) says only that it updates DRAFT metadata in place. A reader who trusts that sentence stops looking. THIS ENTRY MUST CORRECT IT rather than sit beside it.

THE REMEDY IS A CHOICE AND THE ENTRY SHOULD RECORD IT RATHER THAN PICK. (a) Route `editPwa` through `withPwaVersionBump` — but that helper is itself recorded as an AGG-1 divergence BY NAME at JPWB-REG-005:1316 ("a broad transaction constructed to simulate workflow atomicity across two aggregates, at three production call sites"), so extending it to a fourth site is not free. So the forbidden arrangement is: a state carrier on which incompleteness has no declared representation and must therefore be signalled by absence.

WHAT I DROVE, AND WHY EACH PROBE IS THERE. Six ChangePwuState dispatches, each against its OWN freshly-proposed PWU so no probe contaminates the next, every payload key byte-identical except `shapeIntegrityState`:

THE INVENTORY OF COEXISTING REPRESENTATIONS (this is the part the arm rests on):
 (a) `professional_work_objects` — the materialized current state; what every handler reads via `ctx.store.loadObject`.
 (b) `domain_events` — the append-only log; the same units of meaning, re-derivable.
 (c) `professional_work_object_versions` + `outbox_messages` — a version history and a delivery copy.
 (d) the in-memory read-model folds (workProjector, compatibilityProjector, traceabilityProjector, assurance-view, execution-view, pwa-graph). Pure, no durable home.
 (e) ⚠ `EngineHandle.fork()` — a SECOND FULL ENGINE over `SnapshotOverlayStorageAdapter`, running the same handlers, and WRITABLE. This is the only second representation that can be written, and it has a production caller (apps/rph-demo/src/lib/server/authoring-turn.ts:237, `const isolated = canonical.fork();`).

SO I DROVE (e), THE ONLY ONE THAT COULD BREAK THE LIMB. Setup: a canonical PWA with ROOT+OTHER PWU-Types. Fork. Dispatch `EditPwuType` on the FORK renaming OTHER. The fork ACCEPTED it and moved to revision 1 / 9 events; canonical stayed at revision 0 / 7 events / name "Other". CONTROL, the nearest neighbour that must be ACCEPTED: the SAME command shape dispatched on the AUTHORITY moved canonical to revision 1 and name "RENAMED-ON-CANONICAL". So the refusal-to-propagate discriminates: the command is real, it writes when dispatched at the authority, and it does not write when dispatched at the second representation. After both, the two representations genuinely CONTRADICT (shadow says RENAMED-IN-THE-SHADOW, canonical says RENAMED-ON-CANONICAL) and canonical is unmoved.

WHY THIS IS MULTI-SITE AND NOT BY-CONSTRUCTION: the forbidden arrangement is EXPRESSIBLE — a writable second representation exists — and four independent, partial mechanisms are what keep authority singular. None is total:
 S1 packages/rph-engine/src/engine.ts:200 — the ONLY place a second engine is constructed routes its store through the isolating overlay (`store: new SnapshotOverlayStorageAdapter(store)`, grep -c -F = 1). Partial: it governs construction, not what a fork may then do.
 S2 packages/rph-persistence/src/snapshot-overlay-storage-adapter.ts:32/34 — the injected canonical adapter is dereferenced at exactly TWO lines, both READS, both inside the constructor. There is no write path back. Partial: it isolates writes, and says nothing about how a candidate is adopted.

This is the DOC-009 prohibition ("Not: Legacy phase mutation → later copy to RPH") performed rather than quoted. Partial: it is one call site's protocol, and `expectedEventCount` is an OPTIONAL parameter (I drove the omitted case — see limb 4).

WHAT THE LIMB CLAIMS. That an Undertaking's authoritative state IS the Professional Work Objects and the relationships among them - i.e. that no authoritative Undertaking-scoped fact lives anywhere else.

THE POSITIVE HALF IS REAL, GATED, AND I DROVE IT. There is exactly ONE durable object table (`professional_work_objects`, packages/rph-persistence/src/schema.ts), one writer (the command bus), and the object envelope closes the type space: `objectType: ProfessionalWorkObjectTypeSchema` (envelopes.ts:51) admits only the 23 enumerated Professional Work Object types, so nothing that is not a PWO can be persisted as state at all. All 105 command types address one of those 23 (census 1, control 30 / 23-of-23), and the closure is pinned by a committed test with its own accept-and-reject control. Every payload is a `z.strictObject`, so no extra state can ride along: I drove `CreateUndertaking` carrying `intentId` and it was refused RPH_VALIDATION_SCHEMA_FAILED while the byte-identical payload with only that field removed was ACCEPTED - two different outcomes from one field, so the refusal is caused by the field and not by the payload generally. And the Undertaking's work really is carried by PWO relationships: the seeded Undertaking's 13 PWUs each carry `undertakingId`, `intentId` and `pwuTypeId`, and its single root is identified by an absent `parentWorkUnitId`.

THE DIVERGENCE, AND IT IS ONE RELATIONSHIP. The Undertaking -> originating Intent relationship has NO Professional Work Object representation whatsoever. It cannot be written at creation (driven: schema refusal), there is no later command (driven: BindUndertakingIntent / SetUndertakingRootWorkUnit / EditUndertaking all `Unknown command type`), and `intentId` appears on exactly one object type, PROFESSIONAL_WORK_UNIT. So for an Undertaking that has no PWU yet, the binding cannot exist in the object graph - and the shipped host holds it OUTSIDE the graph, in a module-level `const undertakingIntent = new Map<string, string>();` at apps/rph-demo/src/lib/server/workbench.ts:52, written by the create-Undertaking action (routes/undertakings/+page.server.ts:127) and read by `resolveIntentId` (routes/undertakings/[id]/+page.server.ts:498-505). THE LIMB NAMES FOUR THINGS semanticVersion MUST COUNT — meaning, obligation, ASSURANCE REQUIREMENT, or authority. I drove the third one, because it is the only one of the four with a live in-place editing command, and the engine does not count it.

WHAT I DROVE. An ASSURANCE_POLICY was created and ACTIVATED with criterion C1 at severityIfNotMet=MATERIAL, mayBeNotApplicable=true, requiredEvidence=[] and independenceRequirement=NONE. One `EditAssurancePolicy` then rewrote all four: severity MATERIAL -> BLOCKING, mayBeNotApplicable true -> false, a REQUIRED evidence item added with requiredForDispositions='ALL' and mayBeWaived=false, and independence NONE -> DIFFERENT_AGENT. ACCEPTED. The policy's assurance requirements after that dispatch are strictly stricter than before — a subject that would have passed now cannot. AND NO VERSION AXIS MOVED: semanticVersion 1 -> 1, `version` "1.0.0" -> "1.0.0", status ACTIVE throughout. Only `revision` moved, 1 -> 2. A changed assurance requirement was recorded as a mechanical save — the exact arrangement OBJ-2's WHY names ('a meaning change hidden inside a mechanical save').

AND THE CALLER CANNOT FIX IT EVEN IF IT WANTS TO. `EditAssurancePolicyPayloadSchema` (messages.ts:712-731) has no `version` field at all — I dumped its key list off the live `COMMANDS` registry: policyId, name, purpose, rationale, applicableObjectTypes, evaluatedClaimTypes, criteria, evaluatorRole, independenceRequirement, findingDefinitions, waiverRules, requiredEvidence, optionalEvidence, dispositionRules, escalationRules, remediationRules, permittedControlActions, applicability. THE MEANING-CHANGE HALF IS PARTLY HONOURED, AND I SAY SO RATHER THAN SCORING THE LIMB AS DEAD. WHAT CANON REQUIRES. JPWB-DOC-003 §4 OBJ-2, limb 2 (anchor_line 109), verbatim: "`semanticVersion` counts changed meaning, obligation, assurance requirement, or authority." The Canonical Domain Model states the same rule (quoted at JPWB-REG-005:3171): "`semanticVersion` increments only when the meaning, obligations, assurance requirements, or authority of the object changes."

WHAT THE CODE DOES. `EditAssurancePolicy` may rewrite EVERY field of a policy's assurance requirement on an ACTIVE policy, and neither version axis moves.
  · `EDITABLE_PATCH_FIELDS` (packages/rph-application/src/handlers/assurance.ts:268-292) is the authoritative list of what an edit may rewrite, and it contains `criteria`, `requiredEvidence`, `dispositionRules`, `escalationRules`, `waiverRules`, `remediationRules`, `permittedControlActions`, `independenceRequirement` and `applicability` — i.e. the assurance requirement in full.
  · `editAssurancePolicy` (assurance.ts:349) commits `newSemanticVersion: loaded.semanticVersion` at assurance.ts:399. The handler's own docblock at assurance.ts:299 states the disposition in its own words: an edit is "same version, revision++".
  · AND THE CALLER CANNOT FIX IT EVEN IF IT WANTS TO. `EditAssurancePolicyPayloadSchema` (packages/rph-contracts/src/messages.ts:712-732) is a `z.strictObject` with NO `version` key. Derived at runtime off the live `COMMANDS` registry: of 105 registered commands, exactly THREE carry a `version` key — CreatePwa, EditPwa, CreateAssurancePolicy — and the five ASSURANCE_POLICY commands are CreateAssurancePolicy, EditAssurancePolicy, SupersedeAssurancePolicy, SuspendAssurancePolicy, ActivateAssurancePolicy. So neither axis is reachable: the handler will not raise `semanticVersion` and the payload cannot raise `version`.

THE DRIVEN ARRANGEMENT (re-driven at HEAD 2026-08-22, node; scratchpad/ref_obj2_c.mjs). Verbatim stdout:
  commands carrying `version`: CreatePwa, EditPwa, CreateAssurancePolicy (3 of 105)
  CreateAssurancePolicy -> ACCEPTED ; ActivateAssurancePolicy -> ACCEPTED
     ACTIVE v1: revision=1 semanticVersion=1 version="1.0.0" status=ACTIVE
  EditAssurancePolicy (assurance requirement CHANGED: independenceRequirement NONE -> DIFFERENT_AGENT, criterion severityIfNotMet MATERIAL -> BLOCKING, mayBeNotApplicable true -> false, a REQUIRED evidence item added with requiredForDispositions 'ALL' and mayBeWaived false) -> ACCEPTED

  EditAssurancePolicy.safeParse({policyId, version:"2.0.0"}) -> REJECTED: [{"code":"unrecognized_keys","keys":["version"],"path":[],"message":"Unrecognized key: \"version\""}]
  EditAssurancePolicy { version: "2.0.0" } through the bus -> VALIDATION_FAILED | RPH_VALIDATION_SCHEMA_FAILED | Schema validation failed
     after attempting to move `version`: revision=2 semanticVersion=1 version="1.0.0" status=ACTIVE
The policy's assurance requirements after that dispatch are strictly stricter than before — a subject that would have passed now cannot — and the meaning counter did not move. Only `revision` moved, 1 -> 2. This is the arrangement OBJ-2's WHY names: a meaning change hidden inside a mechanical save.

THE CONTROLS THAT MAKE THE ADMISSION ATTRIBUTABLE (same run). (a) THE EDIT PATH IS CAPABLE OF REFUSING: the same command carrying NO change -> REJECTED | RPH_VALIDATION_SEMANTIC_FAILED | "EditAssurancePolicy changes nothing: every field present in the payload already equals the target's current value. Re-issuing would append a second edit event and bump revision for an edit that did not happen." So the acceptance is a missing version bump, not a command that never refuses. (b) A semanticVersion CAN MOVE IN THIS SAME STORE: the INTENT in the same run went 1 -> 2 via ReviseIntent, so the flatness is a property of the ASSURANCE_POLICY path and not of the reader.

THE CENSUS. `grep -rn --include=*.ts -E "semanticVersion \+ 1" packages/*/src apps/*/src | grep -v "\.test\."` -> 4 (intent.ts:167 and kit.ts:807, the two GENERIC helpers reached only when a caller sets `bumpSemanticVersion`; intent.ts:336 a comment; pwa-authoring.ts:178 the one direct raise), combined with `grep -rn --include=*.ts "bumpSemanticVersion: true" packages/rph-application/src/handlers/*.ts | grep -v "\.test\."` -> 2 (decomposition.ts:495, intent.ts:329). Exactly three aggregates can ever raise a semantic version — INTENT, DECOMPOSITION_CONTRACT, PROFESSIONAL_WORK_ARCHITECTURE — and ASSURANCE_POLICY, whose entire content IS an assurance requirement, is not among them.

WHY IT MATTERS, and the filing should say so. `RequestAssuranceAssessment` records `policyVersion` on the assessment and mirrors it onto the completion event, so an assessment can be pinned to "1.0.0" while the requirements that string denotes have been rewritten underneath it. evidence:
THE LIMB NAMES TWO FURTHER AXES AND THEY COME OUT OPPOSITE WAYS, SO I SAY BOTH RATHER THAN AVERAGING THEM.

(a) PAYLOAD-SHAPE VERSION — PRESENT AND DISTINCT BY CONSTRUCTION. `objectEnvelopeShape` (envelopes.ts:48-64) declares `schemaVersion`, `semanticVersion` and `revision` as three separate slots of one `z.strictObject`, each with its own schema alias in common.ts (SchemaVersionSchema:27, SemanticVersionSchema:29, RevisionSchema:31). The command envelope carries `commandSchemaVersion` (envelopes.ts:103) and the event envelope `eventSchemaVersion` (envelopes.ts:144) — separate fields again. OBSERVED: a stored INTENT carried `schemaVersion = 1 | semanticVersion = 1 | revision = 0` as three distinct keys in one object, and the emitted events carried `eventSchemaVersion = 1` as a key of their own. Nothing conflates them: no production site writes one axis from another. The closure is LIVE rather than nominal, which I checked instead of assuming — `EditPwa.payload.safeParse({version:'1.0.1', layout:{...}})` returned REJECTED with `{"code":"unrecognized_keys","keys":["layout"]}`, so the strictObject really does refuse an undeclared key.

(b) CONTRACT-PACKAGE VERSION — NO SHAPE AT ALL, AND THIS IS WHY THE ROW IS SCORED AS IT IS. `ContractVersionSchema` exists at the cited line and is referenced NOWHERE in the repository — not by an envelope, not by an object schema, not by a command or event payload, not by a handler, not by a test. No aggregate, command or event carries a contract-package version in any spelling. The `@janumipwb/rph-contracts` package.json version is the placeholder "0.0.0" and no runtime code reads it. So there is no field, command or event against which 'the contract-package version is a distinct axis' could be enforced, tested, or violated.

AND CANON REALLY DOES ASK FOR FOUR, SO THE ABSENCE IS NOT A SPELLING QUESTION. JPWB-DOC-002 §5 L210-212: 'Four version words carry four distinct meanings, and they are never interchangeable: … **contractVersion** — a package release of the contracts themselves'. DOC-002 L296 cedes to the repository only 'Field names, serialized shapes, and the PLACEMENT of the four version words' — the spelling and the placement, not the existence. OBJ-2's own SCOPE line says the same ('Exact version field spellings are repository shapes'). common.ts:23 even labels its own block 'The version quartet (docs §5 ratify sheet): four distinct fields with distinct meanings' — the repository declares four and builds three. The Ratify Sheet R1 row for '§5-7 Presentation, packages, versions | Views/Projections; packages; four version axes' is still an UNTICKED box, so nobody has ratified the three-axis reduction either.

WHY NOT ENFORCED_BY_CONSTRUCTION. Half the limb would earn that arm; scoring the whole row that way would report the missing axis as satisfied by the present one, which is the same collapse the invariant forbids. Why not DIVERGENT_UNFILED: no behaviour diverges today, because an axis nothing carries cannot be conflated with anything — the honest statement is that the subject is absent, which is what UNENFORCED_NO_SHAPE says.

evidence:
THE LIMB HAS TWO HALVES AND I SCORED THEM SEPARATELY.

HALF ONE — 'an EXPLICIT, TESTED judgment in its handler'. It is explicit in a handful of handlers and silent in the rest, and the silence is load-bearing because the default is 'not semantic'. `advanceStatus`'s option is `readonly bumpSemanticVersion?: boolean;` (kit.ts:730) — OPTIONAL, so a handler that says nothing is read as declaring its command non-semantic. Of the 105 registered command types, exactly 5 carry an explicit positive declaration: ReviseIntent (`bumpSemanticVersion: true`, intent.ts:329), ReviseDecomposition (decomposition.ts:495) and DefinePwuType / EditPwuType / RemovePwuType (via `withPwaVersionBump` at pwa-authoring.ts:483, 734, 818). ZERO command types carry an explicit NEGATIVE declaration — `bumpSemanticVersion: false` occurs nowhere in the repository. Of 42 direct `advanceStatus` call sites exactly 1 mentions the flag at all, against 46 that declare a `precondition` — so on the very same construct, the precondition judgment is universally declared and the semantic judgment is declared once. Twelve commits pass `newSemanticVersion: loaded.semanticVersion` explicitly, which is a token but a mechanical carry-forward rather than a stated judgment. And 'TESTED' is thinner still: ten assertion sites in the whole repository assert a semanticVersion VALUE, of which the three that pin 'it did not move' (command-reissue-guard.test.ts:257, decomposition-revise-conservation.test.ts:175, dwp03-precondition-coverage.test.ts:364) all pin it after a REFUSED command, and the one that pins a presentation change leaving semantics alone (properties.test.ts:313) runs on `applyPresentationChange`, which has ZERO production callers. So NO committed test asserts that an ACCEPTED, non-semantic command leaves semanticVersion unchanged.

HALF TWO — 'objective, boundary, obligation, and decomposition changes are semantic'. DECOMPOSITION is honoured (ReviseDecomposition bumps the contract, decomposition.ts:495). OBLIGATION is honoured at the allocation level (`HONOURED_REVISION_FIELDS` = obligationAllocations, constraintPropagations on the same bumping path). BOUNDARY is honoured only vicariously: EditPwuType may change `executionBoundary`/`boundaryContract` and bumps the owning PWA while the PWU_TYPE that actually changed stays at semanticVersion 1 (driven — see the transcript). OBJECTIVE IS THE ONE THAT DIVERGES OUTRIGHT, AND ITS HANDLER DECLARES THE OPPOSITE JUDGMENT IN SO MANY WORDS. `formalizeIntent` (intent.ts:228-261) has a `mutate` that writes `formalizedObjective`, `desiredOutcomes`, `successConditions`, `nonGoals`, `ambiguityIds`, `constraintIds` and `stakeholderIds` onto the object, and the cited comment states its ruling: 'FORMALIZED is not a material change, so this command does not bump (no bumpSemanticVersion)'. DRIVEN: FormalizeIntent carrying a formalizedObjective and desired outcomes was ACCEPTED and left the intent at revision=3, semanticVersion=1. Canon's limb says objective changes ARE semantic; the handler's explicit judgment says this one is not. So the shape canon asks for — an explicit judgment in the handler — is genuinely present here, and it is WRONG.

WHY THIS IS FILED AND NOT UNFILED. REG-F-009 in JPWB-REG-005 is exactly this finding: '`FormalizeIntent` does not increment the semantic version its ratified rule says it does … formalization persists `formalizedObjective`, `desiredOutcomes`, `successConditions`, `nonGoals`, and stakeholder/constraint references — a material change by any reading — and an approval taken before it remains valid afterwards.' Status OPEN, 'Recorded, not fixed … remediation unscheduled'. It is restated in-repo at execrem-wp16-enforcement-observed.test.ts:687-690 ('A FORMALIZED INTENT IS AT v1, NOT v2, AND THAT IS A FINDING RATHER THAN A FIXTURE DETAIL … only `reviseIntent` does. See REG-F-009'). That is a filing of the divergence, so this row is PARTIAL_DIVERGENT_FILED rather than DIVERGENT_UNFILED — but the filing covers ONE command, and the declaration-discipline gap it exemplifies (100 of 105 commands judging by silence, no test pinning a negative judgment) is not filed anywhere, which is what `owed` records.

enforcing_anchor: Redefining a PWU Type materially edits the PWA's graph
evidence:
THE LIMB NAMES THREE CLASSES THAT MUST NOT BE SEMANTIC. ONE IS HONOURED; TWO ARE VIOLATED, AND I DROVE BOTH VIOLATIONS.

RETRIES — HONOURED. Driven: a plan taken to ACTIVE, its step STARTED then FAILED, then `RetryExecutionStep` -> ACCEPTED, plan revision 4 -> 5, semanticVersion 1 -> 1. No execution handler reaches a bump: `execution.ts:1020` passes `newSemanticVersion: loaded.semanticVersion` and EXECUTION_PLAN is not one of the three types that can ever raise a version.

FORMATTING — VIOLATED, DRIVEN. `EditPwuType { pwuTypeId, name: 'Root (renamed)' }` — a payload carrying ONE field, a human-readable display name, and nothing else — was ACCEPTED and raised the owning PWA's semanticVersion from 4 to 5. Canon's own OBJ-3 NON-EXAMPLE says display names 'are encouraged — they simply are not identity'; presentation.ts:1-4 in this repository states the rule this limb carries: 'A presentation/layout change … MUST NOT alter an object's semantic version or its assurance state.' The renamed PWU_TYPE itself stayed at semanticVersion 1; it is the PWA — the object a floor review BINDS — whose version moved for a cosmetic edit.

LAYOUT MOVES / NODE ORDERING — VIOLATED, DRIVEN. `EditPwuType { pwuTypeId, permittedChildTypeIds: [C2, C1] }` — the SAME SET of child type ids in reversed ORDER — was ACCEPTED and raised the PWA from 5 to 6. `permittedChildTypeIds` is 'the authoritative flat edge list (render/projections consume it)' (pwa-authoring.ts:442) and nothing reads its ORDER as meaning: every production consumer takes `.length` or set membership (pwa-authoring.ts:283, :764, :860). presentation.ts names this exact class verbatim — 'canvas position, NODE ORDERING, a display-only revision bump'.

THE MECHANISM, AND WHY IT CANNOT DISCRIMINATE. `withPwaVersionBump` wraps definePwuType/editPwuType/removePwuType UNCONDITIONALLY; the cited comment declares the judgment for the whole command ('Redefining a PWU Type materially edits the PWA's graph') and `bumpPwaSemanticVersion` (pwa-authoring.ts:125-199) never inspects WHICH field changed. Its docblock says the bump exists so that floor-gate's `versionOk` (`rec?.version === opts.subjectVersion`) can catch a PWU Type 'smuggled into' a reviewed graph. The consequence of not discriminating is that the same guard now invalidates a satisfied floor review because someone fixed a typo in a node's label.

THE CONSEQUENCE IS THE INVERSE OF THE ONE THE MECHANISM WAS BUILT FOR, AND THE VERSION CANNOT TELL THE TWO APART. CONTROL E in my run: `EditPwuType { completionRule: 'ALL_CHILDREN_COMPLETE' }` — a genuinely material change — raised the PWA 6 -> 7, the same single increment the rename produced. A reader of the PWA's version history sees four identical +1 steps and cannot distinguish 'a type was renamed' from 'the completion rule changed'; the events do not help either, because every bump emits the same `PwaEdited` with payload `{pwaId}` and nothing else (transcript below).

THE ABSENCE HALF IS REAL AND I AM NOT USING IT TO SOFTEN THIS. There is no persisted layout field anywhere — `layout`/`canvas`/`position` occur zero times across packages/rph-contracts/src, and the strict payload schemas actively refuse one (`EditPwa.safeParse` with a `layout` key -> unrecognized_keys). So a DEDICATED layout command cannot violate this limb. REG-F-<next> - The PWA's semantic version is raised by command NAME, never by field: a display-name-only edit and a pure reordering of `permittedChildTypeIds` each increment a meaning counter, indistinguishably from a genuine boundary or completion-rule change.

WHAT CANON REQUIRES. JPWB-DOC-003 §3 OBJ-2 (anchor_line 109): "`semanticVersion` counts changed meaning, obligation, assurance requirement, or authority... Whether a given command is semantic is an explicit, tested judgment in its handler - objective, boundary, obligation, and decomposition changes are semantic; retries, layout moves, and formatting are not." Limb 5 is the final clause. LYR-3 states the same rule for presentation: "No presentation operation may change semantic state or increment a semantic version."

WHAT THE CODE DOES. `withPwaVersionBump` (packages/rph-application/src/handlers/pwa-authoring.ts:200, wrapping `bumpPwaSemanticVersion` at :147-199) is called at three production sites - pwa-authoring.ts:483 (DefinePwuType), :734 (EditPwuType), :818 (RemovePwuType) - none of which passes a field filter. `bumpPwaSemanticVersion(ctx, command, pwaId)` inspects no field at all: it loads the PWA and writes `newSemanticVersion = loaded.semanticVersion + 1` unconditionally. The judgment OBJ-2 demands be "explicit and tested in its handler" is asserted in the docblock - "Material graph edits raise the PWA's semantic version", "because its PWU-Type graph was materially edited" (pwa-authoring.ts:120, :126) - and never performed. `packages/rph-domain/src/presentation.ts:1-4` names this exact class in the repository's own words ("A presentation/layout change - canvas position, node ordering, a display-only revision bump - MUST NOT alter an object's semantic version") and its two predicates `isPresentationOnlyChange` / `applyPresentationChange` are DEAD: zero production callers, classified DEAD_BY_DESIGN at verif/dead-kernel-census.test.ts:180,184.

THE DRIVEN ARRANGEMENT (node, real engine, one store). Verbatim:
  setup: PWA revision=3 semanticVersion=4 ; ROOT permittedChildTypeIds = ["pwut_...W46","pwut_...W47"]
  PROBE A ("formatting"): EditPwuType { name: "Root (renamed)" } -> ACCEPTED ; PWA semanticVersion 4 -> 5 ; the PWU_TYPE that was actually renamed stays at semanticVersion 1
  PROBE B ("layout moves" / node ordering): EditPwuType { permittedChildTypeIds: [C2, C1] } - the same SET, reversed ORDER -> ACCEPTED ; PWA semanticVersion 5 -> 6

FOUR CONTROLS, ALL IN THE SAME RUN.
  C (the path discriminates, so the bump is not fired by every dispatch): the same rename re-issued verbatim -> REJECTED | RPH_VALIDATION_SEMANTIC_FAILED | "EditPwuType changes nothing: every field present in the payload already equals the target's current value. Re-issuing would append a second edit event and bump revision for an edit that did not happen." PWA stays at 6.
  D (the bump is a property of the PWU-Type path, not of editing in general): EditPwa { name: "A renamed" } -> ACCEPTED ; PWA semanticVersion 6 -> 6.
  E (the command CAN carry a genuinely material change): EditPwuType { completionRule: "ALL_CHILDREN_COMPLETE" } -> ACCEPTED ; PWA semanticVersion 6 -> 7 - THE SAME +1 AS THE RENAME.
  E' (same comparison in a second fixture): a real boundary change (INTERNAL -> DELEGATED_EXTERNAL with a boundaryContract) takes the PWA 2 -> 3, and a display-name-only edit on the same type takes it 3 -> 4. A BOUNDARY change and a RENAME are the same increment.

AND THE GOVERNED STREAM CANNOT DISAMBIGUATE THEM EITHER. Every bump emits the same event: `PwaEdited rev=4 cmd=c-12#pwa-version payload={"pwaId":"pwa_..."}`, `rev=5 cmd=c-15#pwa-version {"pwaId":...}`, `rev=7 cmd=c-21#pwa-version {"pwaId":...}` - the two cosmetic bumps and the material one are byte-identical apart from the derived command id. Nothing downstream can tell a rename from a completion-rule change.

THE LIVE CONSEQUENCE, WHICH IS THE MECHANISM'S OWN PURPOSE FIRED IN THE WRONG DIRECTION. `floor-gate.ts`'s `versionOk` check (`rec?.version === opts.subjectVersion`) invalidates a SATISFIED PWA floor review whenever the PWA's semanticVersion moves. The bump exists precisely to make that check bite on material edits (HARMONIZATION-LOG.md:604,634 record the stale-floor defect it was built to fix). Because it fires on cosmetic edits too, renaming a PWU Type invalidates a completed floor review and blocks publication until the review is redone - a presentation operation changing a governed gate's outcome.

WHY RPH-PRJ-004 IS NOT A FILING FOR THIS. The register row RPH-PRJ-004 (packages/rph-domain/src/enforcement-register.ts:2711-2731) carries this exact canonAnchor and disposes it as "THE SUBJECT DOES NOT EXIST" on a census of DEDICATED presentation commands and presentation field spellings ("position, layout, canvas, viewport, collapse, ordering") across the 100-command vocabulary. That census is correct in its own terms and does not cover a general-purpose edit command carrying a presentation-only patch. The row should gain a cross-reference to this entry rather than be left reading as coverage; it is satisfied by absence of a subject it defined too narrowly.

REMEDY. Gate the bump on a declared MATERIAL-FIELD SET - the analogue of `decomposition.ts`'s `HONOURED_REVISION_FIELDS` - consulted per payload rather than per command name, so `name`/`purpose` and a pure permutation of a set-valued field leave the PWA's semanticVersion still while boundary, obligation, completion-rule and child-rule changes move it. Red-first: PROBE A and PROBE B must hold the version, while CONTROL E still bumps and CONTROL C still refuses. Note that the red test for PROBE A/B would be this repository's FIRST test pinning a NEGATIVE semantic judgment on an ACCEPTED command (see limb:OBJ-2:4).

SHARED FILING. limb:OBJ-2:2 is the same defect in the opposite direction - `EditAssurancePolicy` rewriting every field of an ACTIVE policy's assurance requirement without moving `semanticVersion`. One rule is broken twice: the bump decision is made by command name and never by field, so it over-counts here and under-counts there. A single materiality mechanism (a per-command semantic-field declaration consulted at every version-write site) closes both, and one entry should carry both directions.

WHAT THE LIMB FORBIDS: malformed OR invalid validator output (a) mutating authoritative state, or (b) creating authoritative findings.

THE ENFORCED HALF IS REAL AND I DROVE IT — THREE MECHANISMS THAT COMPOSE, NONE TOTAL ALONE.
  (i) THE SCHEMA. `ValidatorResultSchema` is a z.strictObject of sixteen required §20 keys with `dispositionRecommendation` bound to a five-value ratified enum. Driven: a §20 required field omitted (`claimResults`) -> VALIDATION_FAILED; an undeclared extra key -> VALIDATION_FAILED; `dispositionRecommendation: 'looks reasonable'` (unparsed prose, canon's own non-example) -> VALIDATION_FAILED; the whole validatorResult replaced by a bare string -> VALIDATION_FAILED. In EVERY case assessmentState stayed ASSESSING and the store's event count did not move (18 -> 18 etc.). NO MUTATION.
  (ii) THE SEMANTIC LIMB, which is the cited site and the register's own carrier. `parseCompletion` refuses a schema-valid result that names a subject and no semantic version for it: REJECTED / RPH_VALIDATOR_OUTPUT_INVALID, assessmentState unchanged. The docblock at 1815-1821 explains why the schema cannot say this ('a shape check is not an invariant check') and records that the hole was found by mutation.
  (iii) BY CONSTRUCTION, the second clause. `completeAssuranceAssessment` builds `observationIds` from the AGGREGATE (`next.observationIds ?? []`), never from `validatorResult.observations`. Driven: a schema-valid completion whose `observations` array carried `[{statement:'could be improved', severity:'CRITICAL'}]` was ACCEPTED and created ZERO AssuranceObservationRecorded events (0 -> 0). A validator's proposed findings cannot become authoritative findings on this path at all — which also means `ProposedAssuranceObservationSchema = z.record(z.string(), z.unknown())` being fully opaque costs nothing here.
CONTROL, the nearest neighbour that MUST be accepted: a well-formed §20 ValidatorResult with dispositionRecommendation SATISFIED -> ACCEPTED, assessmentState SATISFIED, event count 25 -> 26. So the refusals discriminate.

THE DIVERGENT HALF, DRIVEN AGAINST THE SYSTEM'S OWN DEFINITION OF 'INVALID'. `classifyValidatorResult` (packages/rph-assurance/src/assurance-rules.ts:257-283) IS the codebase's definition of invalid validator output — eight BOUNDARY_REJECTED classes. I ran the classifier one class at a time, then put the SAME arrangement on the wire. FOUR classes the kernel calls INVALID are ADMITTED by the engine and each MUTATES AUTHORITATIVE STATE, ASSESSING -> SATISFIED:
  D1 required criteria missing (`claimResults: []`) — kernel: BOUNDARY_REJECTED 'required criteria missing'; engine: ACCEPTED -> SATISFIED.
  D2 policy version mismatch (`policyVersion: '9.9.9'`) — kernel: BOUNDARY_REJECTED RPH_POLICY_VERSION_MISMATCH; engine: ACCEPTED -> SATISFIED.
  D3 subject version mismatch (verdict binds v99, the assessment was created for v1) — kernel: BOUNDARY_REJECTED RPH_SUBJECT_VERSION_MISMATCH; engine: ACCEPTED -> SATISFIED.
  D4 a validatorId naming a validator never registered — the DISABLED arm at assurance.ts:2145 fires only on a registered-and-disabled entry; engine: ACCEPTED -> SATISFIED.
The control D0 (a genuinely VALID result with one answered claim) was ACCEPTED, so the pass is not vacuous.

WHY PARTIAL AND NOT UNENFORCED: two of the limb's three attack surfaces are genuinely closed (literal malformation; finding creation) and one class of semantic invalidity is genuinely refused at the cited site. WHY DIVERGENT AND NOT ENFORCED: four kernel-defined invalidity classes reach authoritative state. WHY FILED: every one of the four is already on the record, verbatim, and RPH-CON-005's own words are this limb's consequent.

WHAT CANON REQUIRES. JPWB-DOC-003 §8 ASR-11, limb 2 (anchor_line 285), verbatim: "Malformed or invalid validator output can never mutate authoritative state or create authoritative findings;". The SECOND consequent — "or create authoritative findings" — is the one that fails.

WHAT THE CODE DOES. The engine has its own definition of invalid validator output — `classifyValidatorResult` (packages/rph-assurance/src/assurance-rules.ts) with eight BOUNDARY_REJECTED classes. On the FLOOR RECORDING PATH that verdict is consulted for the DISPOSITION field and for nothing else, and the validator's proposed observations are rehydrated into authoritative ASSURANCE_OBSERVATION objects regardless.
  · packages/rph-assurance/src/recording.ts:102 — `if (po.resultClass === 'MISSING') continue;` — is the ONLY consultation of `po.resultClass` in the whole file. :104 then builds `const observations: RecordableObservation[] = (r?.observations ?? []).map(...)` UNCONDITIONALLY.
  · recording.ts:130, in the SAME function, `disposition: toRecordable(po.disposition)` DOES consult the boundary outcome — `toRecordable` (recording.ts:82) folds VALIDATOR_FAILED / BOUNDARY_REJECTED / MISSING to INCONCLUSIVE. The invalidity verdict is in hand at the point of use, is spent on one field and not the other.
  · Upstream, packages/rph-assurance/src/floor.ts:313 `observations.push(...r.observations)` runs UNCONDITIONALLY and BEFORE the classification; floor.ts:347 sets `resultClass: klass.klass`.
  · Downstream, packages/rph-engine/src/record-assurance.ts:93 (`recordAssuranceRecordingPlan`) turns each rehydrated observation into a `RecordAssuranceObservation` dispatch at :146. Production caller: apps/rph-demo/src/lib/server/floor.ts:332 (`runFloorAndPlanRecording`) and :337 (`recordAssuranceRecordingPlan`).

⚠ THE CODE ASSERTS THE LIMB'S CONSEQUENT AT THE LINE WHERE IT FAILS, and the entry should quote it. packages/rph-assurance/src/floor.ts:336, verbatim at HEAD: `aggDisposition = 'INCONCLUSIVE'; // malformed result cannot create an authoritative finding → blocks.` The observations were already pushed at :313 and are rehydrated at recording.ts:104 regardless. The recording.ts docblock above :92 goes further and states the leak as an intention: "rehydrates each recorded policy with its Validator result's observations ... so the persisted ASSURANCE_OBSERVATIONs are faithful to exactly what the Validator proposed."

THE DRIVEN ARRANGEMENT (re-driven at HEAD 2026-08-22, node, real engine + real floor registry, de minimis floor plan; scratchpad/v4_asr11_confirm.mjs). A validator result with `policyVersion: '9.9.9'` against a policy at its real version — which `classifyValidatorResult` returns BOUNDARY_REJECTED / RPH_POLICY_VERSION_MISMATCH for — carrying one proposed observation `{code:'FINDING', severity:'CRITICAL', statement:'MARK the subject is defective'}`.      recordedDispositions = ["INCONCLUSIVE","INCONCLUSIVE"]
     observationIds returned = 2
     OBJECT obs_00000000000000000000000002 type=ASSURANCE_OBSERVATION severity=CRITICAL disposition=OPEN statement="MARK the subject is defective" observationType=POLICY_VIOLATION
     OBJECT obs_00000000000000000000000004 type=ASSURANCE_OBSERVATION severity=CRITICAL disposition=OPEN statement="MARK the subject is defective" observationType=POLICY_VIOLATION
TWO CONTROLS, BOTH REQUIRED AND BOTH OBSERVED IN THE SAME RUN. CONTROL-VALID (identical result, correct policyVersion): `recordedDispositions = ["REJECTED","REJECTED"]`, `observationIds returned = 2`, the same two ASSURANCE_OBSERVATION objects — so invalidity changed the DISPOSITION and left the findings byte-identical. CONTROL-MISSING (no validator registered, resultClass MISSING): `recordedDispositions = []`, `observationIds returned = 0` — the path can return zero, so the pass is not vacuous. The same leak reproduces for the `required criteria missing` and `SATISFIED with an unmet mandatory criterion` boundary classes (scratchpad/r_asr11_c.mjs).

WHY IT MATTERS. These are materialized governed objects with `disposition=OPEN` and `severity=CRITICAL` — precisely the class that Gate C (`rejectForeclosedDisposition`, packages/rph-application/src/handlers/assurance.ts:1901) forecloses positive dispositions on. THE LIMB SAYS CORRECTIONS CREATE SUCCESSORS WITH SUPERSESSION LINKS. I DROVE TWO OF THE FIVE SUPERSEDE COMMANDS INTO ACCEPTING A SUPERSESSION WITH NO SUCCESSOR AT ALL, AND A THIRD DOES THE SAME BY ITS OWN RECORD.

ADMISSION A — A SUPERSESSION WHOSE SUCCESSOR IS FICTION. `SupersedePwu` (pwu.ts:937-947) supplies no `guard`; it copies `supersedingWorkUnitId` straight into the emitted event. Driven: `SupersedePwu A -> pwu_01ARZ3NDEKTSV4RRFFQ69G8D99` (an id created nowhere) -> **ACCEPTED**. The PWU is now SUPERSEDED, `successor exists in store? = false`, the object state carries NO key naming a successor, and the only carrier is the event payload `{"supersedingWorkUnitId":"pwu_...D99","workLifecycleState":"SUPERSEDED"}` — a link to nothing.

ADMISSION B — A SUPERSESSION WITH NO LINK WHATSOEVER. `SupersedeAssurancePolicyPayloadSchema` (packages/rph-contracts/src/messages.ts:733-736) types `supersededByPolicyId: z.string().optional()`. Driven: `SupersedeAssurancePolicy POL {no supersededByPolicyId}` -> **ACCEPTED**; POL status = SUPERSEDED; `tags = []`; no state key matching /supersed|successor|replac/; and the persisted `AssurancePolicySuperseded` payload is `{"policyId":"pol_...B03"}` — the successor field is not merely dangling, it is ABSENT. The record now says 'this policy was replaced' and names nothing that replaced it. The handler's own docblock (assurance.ts:405-406) presupposes the opposite: "retire a policy version (ACTIVE|SUSPENDED -> SUPERSEDED) **when a successor replaces it**. The successor id (if given) is recorded as a `superseded-by:<id>` tag."

AND THE LINK IS NOT RESOLVED EVEN WHEN GIVEN. `SupersedeAssurancePolicy POL2 -> names successor POL` was ACCEPTED although POL is ITSELF already SUPERSEDED — the record now chains a live policy to a dead one with no check.

WHAT IS ENFORCED, so this is not read as total: `SupersedeIntent` (intent.ts:384-437) REQUIRES the successor, LOADS it, and refuses three ways — nonexistent, wrong type, and self. `SupersedeExecutionPlan` (execution.ts:642-652) resolves the successor and additionally requires it to sit on the SAME PWU. So two of five hold the line and three do not.

THE OBJECT-SIDE LINK IS ALSO A DECLARED-AND-UNWRITTEN FIELD. `IntentObject` declares `supersedesIntentId: z.string().optional()` (packages/rph-contracts/src/objects.ts:418, and IntentObject.json:288) and NOTHING writes it — after a successful SupersedeIntent I inspected both objects: `I1 state keys mentioning supersede = []`, `I2 state keys mentioning supersede = []`. WHAT CANON REQUIRES. JPWB-DOC-003 §9 PER-8, limb 3 (anchor_line 365), verbatim: "corrections create successors with supersession links."

WHAT THE CODE DOES. Of the five supersede commands, two hold the line and three do not; on two of them the LINK half of the limb is unperformed, and on four of five the link exists only as an event field with no object carrier.

ADMISSION A — A SUPERSESSION WHOSE SUCCESSOR IS FICTION. `supersedePwu` (packages/rph-application/src/handlers/pwu.ts:937-947) supplies no `guard`; it copies `supersedingWorkUnitId` straight into the emitted event at pwu.ts:943 and never loads the object that id names.
ADMISSION B — A SUPERSESSION WITH NO LINK WHATSOEVER. `SupersedeAssurancePolicyPayloadSchema` (packages/rph-contracts/src/messages.ts:733-736) types `supersededByPolicyId: z.string().optional()`. The handler's own docblock (assurance.ts:405-406) presupposes the opposite: "retire a policy version (ACTIVE|SUSPENDED -> SUPERSEDED) **when a successor replaces it**.   CONTROL — the same command shape naming a REAL successor: SupersedePwu B -> the real PWU A -> ACCEPTED. Both accepted; the engine does not distinguish a real successor from a fictional one on this command.
  SIBLING CONTROL — the command that DOES resolve its successor: SupersedeIntent INT -> int_...NEVER_CREATED -> REJECTED | RPH_VALIDATION_SEMANTIC_FAILED | "SupersedeIntent requires an existing INTENT as the superseding intent, and int_01ARZ3NDEKTSV4RRFFQ69G8D04 is not stored.   >>> SupersedeAssurancePolicy POL {no supersededByPolicyId} -> ACCEPTED
  POL status = SUPERSEDED | tags = [] | any state key naming a successor = []
  POL events = ["AssurancePolicyCreated","AssurancePolicyActivated","AssurancePolicySuperseded"] | AssurancePolicySuperseded payload = {"policyId":"pol_01ARZ3NDEKTSV4RRFFQ69G8B03"}

The governed record now says "this policy was replaced" and names nothing that replaced it; and a PWU is SUPERSEDED — a terminal state — by a work unit that does not exist.

THE OBJECT-SIDE CARRIER IS DECLARED AND UNWRITTEN. `IntentObject` declares `supersedesIntentId: z.string().optional()` (packages/rph-contracts/src/objects.ts:418, and schemas/objects/IntentObject.json:288) and NOTHING writes it. THIS LIMB'S SUBJECT IS THE FIXING MECHANISM, NOT THE ARRANGEMENT. The repository HAS one — `TRACE_DIRECTIONALITY` (packages/rph-domain/src/traceability.ts:27-92), a 17-relation table that fixes exactly what this limb says, correctly: `SUPPORTS: { source: ['EVIDENCE','ASSURANCE_ASSESSMENT'], target: ['CLAIM'] }` (:51) and `VERIFIES: { source: ['ASSURANCE_ASSESSMENT'], target: ['CLAIM','PROFESSIONAL_WORK_UNIT','BASELINE'] }` (:53-56). THE PREDICATE THAT READS THE TABLE CANNOT FAIL IN PRODUCTION, AND I PROVED IT RATHER THAN ASSERTING IT.

PROOF 1 — THE ARGUMENTS ARE CONSTANTS AT THE ONLY REACHABLE CALL SITE. `validateLinkDirectionality` has exactly one non-test caller: `TraceGraph.addLink` at traceability.ts:151, and `addLink` has exactly one non-test caller: `supportsGraph` (packages/rph-application/src/handlers/assurance.ts:585-606), reached from `invalidateEvidence` at assurance.ts:642. Read the call: `graph.addNode({ id: evidenceId, objectType: EVIDENCE })` (:596), `graph.addNode({ id: claimId, objectType: CLAIM })` (:597), `graph.addLink({ …, relation: 'SUPPORTS', … })` (:598-603). All three arguments the predicate receives — relation, source type, target type — are the literals 'SUPPORTS', 'EVIDENCE', 'CLAIM' on every execution. `validateLinkDirectionality('SUPPORTS','EVIDENCE','CLAIM')` is `{ok:true}` unconditionally. THE ONE CHECK THAT FIXES SUPPORT AND VERIFICATION BY TYPE IS ASKED THE SAME QUESTION EVERY TIME, AND IT IS THE ANSWER 'YES'.

PROOF 2 — I DROVE THE VIOLATING ARRANGEMENT THROUGH THAT EXACT PREDICATE AND IT PASSED. `ProposeEvidence` with `supportsClaimIds:[<a PROFESSIONAL_WORK_UNIT>]` → ACCEPTED; `InvalidateEvidence` on it → ACCEPTED, and it emitted `EvidenceInvalidated{affectedClaimIds:["pwu_01ARZ3NDEKTSV4RRFFQ69GR201"]}`. Producing that value REQUIRED `supportsGraph` to run `addNode({id: <the PWU>, objectType: CLAIM})` — fabricating the target's type — and then `addLink` to put a SUPPORTS edge through `validateLinkDirectionality`, which returned ok. THE SAME PREDICATE, ASKED THE TRUE TYPES IN THE SAME SESSION, REFUSES: `validateLinkDirectionality('SUPPORTS','EVIDENCE','PROFESSIONAL_WORK_UNIT')` -> `{"ok":false,"reason":"SUPPORTS target must be one of CLAIM, got PROFESSIONAL_WORK_UNIT"}`. The rule is correct, alive, and never asked the question that would make it fire.

PROOF 3 — A SECOND, INDEPENDENT DEADNESS MECHANISM. `addLink` validates only `if (s && t)` (traceability.ts:150): when either endpoint is not a registered node, the check is SKIPPED ENTIRELY and the link is pushed. Driven: `new TraceGraph().addLink({id:'l1',relation:'SUPPORTS',from:'a',to:'b'})` with no `addNode` → no throw, and `outgoing('a')` returns the link. The handler's own docblock at assurance.ts:582-583 is aware of this — "omitting them would silently skip the check that makes the graph trustworthy" — and its remedy is to supply the types itself, as constants, which is proof 1.

Two handler-local filters do fix a type: assurance.ts:704 `if (e.aggregateType === EVIDENCE)` fixes the ORIGIN of the claim-status support path, and pwu.ts:1362 fixes the ORIGIN of a PWU's assurance verdict to ASSURANCE_ASSESSMENT (driven, scored at limb:REL-2:2). A rule that holds where a particular handler happens to have written it is not a rule fixed by type; it is 25 separate rules, and this limb's own artifact for stating it once is the table that nothing asks.

evidence:
A FOUR-WAY NEGATIVE. Scored one clause at a time; three hold, one is admitted on the wire.

(a) 'NEVER MUTATE PROFESSIONAL STATE' — HOLDS, by construction and driven. Exactly ONE payload in the entire message surface carries a validator's output (messages.ts:223, CompleteAssuranceAssessment), its targetAggregateType is ASSURANCE_ASSESSMENT, and `commitState` (kit.ts:401) writes exactly one `args.aggregateId` per dispatch — the engine has no multi-aggregate write. DRIVEN: before/after a completion, the PWU is revision 0 -> 0, semanticVersion 1 -> 1, assuranceState UNASSESSED -> UNASSESSED, workLifecycleState PROPOSED -> PROPOSED; the CLAIM stays OPEN; the EVIDENCE stays ADMISSIBLE; and the event log shows the dispatch wrote the assessment aggregate and nothing else. Corroborated the other way: `command-bus.ts` resolves one handler per dispatch and the only event fan-out is a read-only `EventSubscriber = (event) => void`, so no accepted validator result can mint a second command (the register states this at enforcement-register.ts:1069-1072 for RPH-ASR-001).

(b) 'NEVER RETURN ONLY PROSE' — HOLDS. There is no free-text verdict channel: the verdict is `dispositionRecommendation`, enum-bound; `limitations` and `residualUncertainty` are string arrays that no gate and no projection treats as a verdict. Driven negatively: a non-enum recommendation ('WAIVED') dies at the schema.

(c) 'NEVER RETURN ONLY PASS-FAIL' — ⚠ ADMITTED, AND THIS IS THE ROW'S FINDING. DRIVEN: a completion in which EVERY content field is empty — claimResults [], observations [], evidenceConsideredIds [], evidenceRejected [], residualUncertainty [], limitations [], recommendedControlActions [] — was ACCEPTED and the assessment settled SATISFIED. What remains on such a result is identity (validatorId/version, policyId/version, assessmentId, subject + version) plus ONE enum value. That is the bare verdict canon forbids; the only thing standing between it and literal pass/fail is that the enum has five members rather than two, and nothing in the engine requires a single one of the content fields to be non-empty. The rule IS honoured one layer down, in the FLOOR kernel's own `ValidatorResult` (packages/rph-assurance/src/floor.ts:89-115), whose `criteria: readonly FloorCriterion[]` is a typed CriterionResult array and whose docblock states the canon clause verbatim — but that typed criterion detail is explicitly dropped at the wire boundary, which is the filed divergence.

(d) 'NEVER RETURN UNSCOPED CONFIDENCE' — VACUOUSLY HELD, and I will not dress that up as enforcement. `ValidatorResultSchema` has no confidence field at all, so a validator cannot return confidence of any kind. `AssuranceAssessment.confidence` exists (objects.ts:569) and no production line writes it; the only payload that could carry one, AssuranceAssessmentSatisfiedPayloadSchema (messages.ts:908), belongs to an event this engine never emits. See census.

(e) 'VALIDATOR OUTPUT NEVER GRANTS PERMISSIONS' — HOLDS, driven at full strength. `ControlActionSchema` DOES include ACCEPT and PROMOTE_BASELINE, so a validator can literally recommend the acts limb 3 reserves. Two independent barriers, both driven: Gate B (assurance.ts:1862) refuses a recommendation outside the policy's permitted set; and when the policy DOES permit it — I seeded permittedControlActions ['CONTINUE','ACCEPT','PROMOTE_BASELINE'], the validator recommended ACCEPT and PROMOTE_BASELINE, and the AssuranceAssessmentCompleted event recorded both — PromoteBaseline citing that assessment was still REJECTED with NO_EFFECTIVE_PROMOTION_DECISION until a Governance Decision existed. The recommendation is recorded and read by exactly one consumer, the read-model (rph-projections/src/assurance-view.ts:263, field `controlActions`); nothing executes it.

WHAT CANON REQUIRES. JPWB-DOC-003 §8 ASR-2, limb 4 (anchor_line 243): a validator's disposition may not stand "when the disposition contradicts mandatory policy rules". ASR-1 states affirmatively that "Policy applicability and disposition rules are declarative data evaluated by the engine".

WHAT THE CODE DOES. `DispositionRuleSchema` (packages/rph-contracts/src/objects.ts:211-216) declares five fields: disposition, condition, requiredEvidenceIds, forbiddenOpenSeverities, requiredIndependence. Exactly ONE has a production reader. The census over what any production line reads off a MATCHED rule - `grep -rn -F 'dispositionRule?.' packages/ apps/` minus node_modules/dist/.svelte-kit/tests - returns three hits of which only `packages/rph-application/src/handlers/assurance.ts:1901` is executable (`const forbidden = new Set([...floor, ...(dispositionRule?.forbiddenOpenSeverities ?? [])]);`); the other two are comments (assurance.ts:1882, apps/rph-demo/src/lib/server/assurance/demo-policy.ts:14). Gate C, `rejectForeclosedDisposition` (assurance.ts:1872-1912), types its own parameter as `ReadonlyArray<{ disposition?: string; forbiddenOpenSeverities?: readonly string[] }>` (assurance.ts:1874-1876) - it discards `requiredEvidenceIds` at the type boundary.   STEP 3 DIVERGENCE: the SAME matched rule demands evidence ER_MANDATORY_FOR_SATISFIED for SATISFIED; NONE submitted -> ACCEPTED; assessmentState = SATISFIED; event.disposition = "SATISFIED"

STEP 2 therefore proves the engine matched this exact object and read a field off it; STEP 1 proves the field survives persistence verbatim; STEP 3 shows the engine holds it in hand at the moment it accepts and never asks. REG-005:3201 states the general form "AN OPTIONAL POLICY FIELD THAT DEFAULTS TO 'NO CONSTRAINT' IS A GATE SWITCHED OFF BY SILENCE", and REG-D-042 fixed that class by UNIONING the de minimis floor in. This instance is the INVERSE: the author WRITES the constraint, in the ratified field built to carry it, and still gets none. No floor default repairs that; only a reader does. This is the hollow-field shape, not the silence-default shape.

WHAT ARRIVES (the positive controls inside the finding). (1) The `ProfessionalRationaleSummary` is a contracted deliverable the producer returns via `declare_rationale`, threaded into `ReasoningReviewInput.rationale` and rendered FIRST in the judge prompt. (2) Outputs arrive as `ReasoningReviewInput.content`, the serialized PWA graph export (apps/rph-demo/src/lib/server/floor.ts:319-322).

WHAT THE CODE DOES — CONJUNCT (i), THE EXCLUSION. The ONLY channel from the producing turn to the reviewer is `narration: planText()` (apps/rph-demo/src/routes/pwa/[id]/agent/+server.ts:131 and :158), and `planText` is `narrationOf(transcript)` (:115). `narrationOf` (apps/rph-demo/src/lib/server/agent/transcript.ts:34-39) is exactly `.filter((e) => e.role === 'AGENT' && e.kind === 'message')` — `tool_call` and `tool_result` entries are dropped. ⚠ AND THE COMPOSITION ROOT'S OWN COMMENT STATES THE CANON REQUIREMENT AND THEN DOES NOT MEET IT — this is the sharpest fact in the finding and it is new. apps/rph-demo/src/lib/server/floor.ts:323-324, verbatim: "§8.4 orders what Reasoning Review reviews: the contracted rationale summary FIRST, then outputs and tool records, then other observable trace data." The very next lines pass `rationale`, `content` and `narration` — and there is no tool-records field. The input type itself concedes the scope at floor.ts:290-291: "/** The producer's observable narration — §8.4 admits 'other observable trace data'. Never its interior. */ narration?: string;". The slot named "tool records" exists in the comment and in no field.

THE PRODUCT PROMISES THE OPPOSITE, IN TWO PLACES. apps/rph-demo/src/lib/server/agent/system-prompt.ts (rule 8): "An independent assurance reviewer judges your work from this account, the graph itself, and your tool calls — it never sees your private reasoning". apps/rph-demo/src/lib/server/agent/tools.ts:123 (`declare_rationale`'s description): "not a list of what you did (the tool calls already record that)". WAIVED — PRESENT. RequestWaiver / GrantWaiver / DenyWaiver are real commands; WAIVED is an ObservationDisposition, an AssuranceState and a constraint disposition; and `isWaiverApplicable` binds a waiver to an exact policy+criterion+object+semanticVersion.

DEFERRED — NO SHAPE AT ALL, and this is the real hole. There is no deferred coverage class anywhere in the assurance model: no enum member, no field, no command, no view column. evidence:
THE LIMB IS A CAPABILITY CLAIM ABOUT VALIDATION: per-part validity must not be allowed to stand in for joint validity. The engine has exactly such a check and it is a live command-surface refusal.

I BUILT THE ARRANGEMENT PIECE BY PIECE SO THAT EVERY PART WAS INDIVIDUALLY VALID. A parent PWU carrying one MANDATORY OBLIGATION ('Isolate tenant data', obligationType SECURITY, an ORGANIZATIONAL_ROLE authority) — ACCEPTED. Two children, each a well-formed ARCHITECTURE PWU with the parent named, in scope, nothing missing — each ACCEPTED on its own. `ProposeDecomposition{childWorkUnitIds:[K1,K2]}` — ACCEPTED. At that point no object in the store is defective and every dispatch has succeeded. The impossibility is a property of the SET: the mandatory obligation is allocated to no child and retained at no parent, so the composition drops it while each component is faultless.

`ValidateDecomposition{disposition:'VALID'}` then REFUSED with RPH_INVARIANT_VIOLATION and named the joint defect precisely: MISSING_OBLIGATION_ALLOCATION(obl_...). The predicate is `checkDecompositionConservation` (decomposition.ts:262), which folds the parent's first-class OBLIGATION and CONSTRAINT objects against the contract's allocations/retentions/propagations via the kernel `validateObligationConservation` / `validateConstraintPropagation` (rph-domain/src/decomposition.ts:165). Note the SHAPE of the kernel's coverage test — 'for every MANDATORY applicable parent constraint, EVERY relevant child must be dispositioned ... a single uncovered relevant child is a per-child SILENT_CONSTRAINT_DROP'. That is a quantifier over the whole child set; no single child can satisfy or violate it alone. That is precisely 'individually valid parts can be jointly impossible', implemented.

THE CONTROL IS BYTE-ADJACENT AND DISCRIMINATES. The same two children, the same parent, the same rationale, plus `retainedParentObligationIds: [OBL]` — ACCEPTED, and the contract really advanced to status VALID. So the refusal is not firing on the children, nor on the act, nor on the obligation's existence; it fires on the JOINT property and stops firing the moment the joint property holds. A refusal that fired for both would have discriminated nothing.

HONESTLY STATED SCOPE LIMIT: this joint check lives on the DECOMPOSITION plane, and ASR-5's SCOPE line is 'governs assurance design and coverage planning'. Within the ASSURANCE plane proper the joint capability is representable but not enforced — `AssuranceAssessment.subjectObjectIds` is an array, so one assessment CAN take several objects as a joint subject and report an impossibility across them, but no gate requires it and `aggregateAssuranceDisposition` folds per-policy verdicts by strictness rather than testing them for joint satisfiability. So the limb's proposition is realized, with the strongest instance one plane over from where ASR-5 sits.

WHAT CANON REQUIRES. JPWB-DOC-003 §8 ASR-5, limb 6 (anchor_line 257), verbatim: "individually valid parts can be jointly impossible." ASR-5's own SCOPE line places the requirement on the assurance plane — "governs assurance design and coverage planning".

WHAT THE CODE DOES. No predicate in this engine ever tests a CLAIM SET for joint satisfiability. Every assurance predicate over claims is universally quantified one claim at a time, so two claims that cannot both hold are each certified and then jointly certified by one assessment.
  · SITE 1 — `recordClaimAssessment`, packages/rph-application/src/handlers/assurance.ts:840. Its ONLY guard is at :879 and refuses at :885; the guard opens `if (target !== 'SUPPORTED') return null;` and then asks a strictly PER-CLAIM question — whether THIS claim is in `claimsWithAdmissibleEvidence(hctx)`. It asks nothing about the set the claim is joining.
  · SITE 2 — `completeAssuranceAssessment`, assurance.ts:2003. Four gates run on that path (permitted control actions, forbidden open severities, escalation rules, mandatory evidence) and not one of them reads a claim. `claimIds` occurs exactly three times in the file and all three are carriage: persisted at :1385, mirrored onto the requested event at :1418, mirrored onto the completion event at :1699.
  · THE CENSUS THAT EXPLAINS BOTH, re-run at HEAD with its controls in the same file: `grep -c "claimResults" packages/rph-application/src/handlers/assurance.ts` -> 0, against the sibling ValidatorResult fields `subjectObjectIds` -> 16 and `dispositionRecommendation` -> 4 in that SAME file, both of which have driven refusals. `claimResults`'s entire production population outside the schema is four writers that all pass `[]`: packages/rph-engine/src/record-assurance.ts:183, packages/rph-engine/src/reference-undertaking.ts:664 and :1171, apps/rph-demo/src/routes/undertakings/[id]/+page.server.ts:581. `AssuranceAssessmentCompleted` has no claim-result key at all — measured payload keys are assessmentId, assurancePolicyId, policyVersion, subjectObjectIds, subjectSemanticVersions, disposition, evidenceConsideredIds, observationIds, residualUncertainty, recommendedControlActions, validatorId, validatorVersion. So the joint verdict is not merely unchecked; it is unrecorded.

evidence:
THE MODEL DRAWS THE DISTINCTION AND THE ONLY GATE THAT ACTS ON OBSERVATIONS THROWS IT AWAY. This is the 'two separate types is necessary and not sufficient' case, caught in the act.

THE DISTINCTION IS REAL ON THE WIRE. `ObservationTypeSchema` (enums.ts:570) has seven members and they sort cleanly into signals and defects: MEASUREMENT, SHAPE_RISK, RECOMMENDATION on one side; FINDING, POLICY_VIOLATION on the other (CONFLICT and EVIDENCE_DEFICIT straddle). `observationType` is required on both the command payload (messages.ts:354) and the object (objects.ts:583).

THE GATE DISCARDS IT. `openObservationSeverities` (assurance.ts:2092-2110) is the single production consumer of an assessment's observations — memoized and shared by Gate D (escalation) and Gate C (the §10.3 foreclosure). The cited line is its filter, and it reads exactly two fields: `disposition === 'OPEN'` and `typeof o.severity === 'string'`. It then maps to `o.severity` and returns a Set of SEVERITY STRINGS. `observationType` never enters the memo, so no downstream gate can see it.

DRIVEN, WITH THE PAIR THAT DISCRIMINATES.
