THREE CLAUSES, DRIVEN SEPARATELY, AND THEY DO NOT ALL LAND THE SAME WAY.

(a) 'PRINCIPLES MAY LEGITIMATELY CONFLICT' — SUPPORTED. Two directly contradicting observations were both accepted on one assessment: CONFLICT/MATERIAL 'Principle A (testability): the module MUST be split into seams.' and CONFLICT/MATERIAL 'Principle B (cohesion): the module MUST NOT be split. Directly contradicts Principle A.' Both persisted, both OPEN. Likewise two REQUIRED policies reached OPPOSITE verdicts on the same subject — A1 SATISFIED, A2 REJECTED — and both stand. The kernel refuses to average them: `aggregateAssuranceDisposition` (rph-domain/src/aggregate-assurance.ts) is first-match-wins down §28.2's strictness order with 'This must not be reduced to a numerical average' and 'a satisfied advisory policy does not override a rejected blocking policy' transcribed above it.

(b) 'PRESERVED' IN THE WEAK SENSE — SUPPORTED. Re-recording on the SAME observation aggregate with the opposite statement is refused: status=CONFLICT / RPH_REVISION_CONFLICT, and the persisted statement is unchanged. A contradiction cannot be overwritten by its opposite.

(c) 'AS EXPLICIT TENSIONS, NEVER SILENTLY RESOLVED' — FAILS, AND THIS IS THE ROW. There is no tension shape: four candidate ways to say it (`tension`, `conflictsWithObservationId`, `relatedObservationIds`, `unresolvedTensionWith`) were each refused as unrecognized keys by the strictObject, so two conflicting observations cannot even be linked to each other, let alone marked unresolved. Worse, the authoritative record of the assessment shows nothing at all: with BOTH contradicting principles still OPEN, `CompleteAssuranceAssessment{SATISFIED}` was ACCEPTED, the assessment advanced to SATISFIED, and the emitted `AssuranceAssessmentCompleted` carried `observationIds: []` and `residualUncertainty: []`. The object's own `observationIds` is `[]` too.

THE MECHANISM BEHIND THE EMPTY ARRAY, AND IT IS STRUCTURAL, NOT INCIDENTAL. `requestAssuranceAssessment` writes `observationIds: []` (assurance.ts:1388); `recordAssuranceObservation` (assurance.ts:2339) creates the observation as its OWN aggregate and never mutates the assessment; the completion event then reads `next.observationIds ?? []` — the cited line — off an array nothing ever appends to. I checked for a shared builder rather than assuming (EM-3): the only other `observationIds` writers in the tree are `ValidateDecomposition`/`ReviseDecomposition` (decomposition.ts:384-391) and `pwu.ts:850`, which copy a caller-supplied array on a DIFFERENT aggregate. So on the assurance plane `assessment.observationIds` is always empty, and every reader of the completed assessment sees a clean SATISFIED with no trace of the tension that was standing when it was signed.

That is 'silently resolved' in the plainest sense available: the observations survive as orphan aggregates, and the record that a governance decision would consult says the assessment was satisfied and nothing was open.

filing_statement:
REG-F-<next> - Conflicting valid principles cannot be recorded as an explicit tension, and the assessment record is blind to its own observations, so a SATISFIED disposition stands over an unresolved contradiction with nothing in the authoritative record saying so.

WHAT CANON REQUIRES. JPWB-DOC-003 §8.2 ASR-5, limb 8 (anchor_line 257), verbatim: "professional principles may legitimately conflict, and conflicting valid principles are preserved as explicit tensions, never silently resolved".

WHAT THE CODE DOES - TWO CONJUNCTS, ONE ENTRY.

(i) NO TENSION SHAPE EXISTS. `RecordAssuranceObservationPayloadSchema` is a `z.strictObject` with no field for declaring a tension or linking two conflicting observations. Driven at the bus, four candidate keys, all refused: `{"tension":"PRESERVED"}`, `{"conflictsWithObservationId":"aob_..."}`, `{"relatedObservationIds":["aob_..."]}`, `{"unresolvedTensionWith":"aob_..."}` -> each VALIDATION_FAILED with `[{"path":"","code":"unrecognized_keys","message":"Unrecognized key: \"<key>\""}]`. Two observations that directly contradict one another are therefore recordable only as two unrelated aggregates; the relation canon calls "an explicit tension" has no carrier anywhere in the ratified model.

(ii) THE ASSESSMENT RECORD IS BLIND TO ITS OWN OBSERVATIONS. `AssuranceAssessment.observationIds` is born `[]` at `packages/rph-application/src/handlers/assurance.ts:1388` and never appended to. `recordAssuranceObservation` (assurance.ts:2339-2401) mints a separate OBSERVATION aggregate carrying a back-pointer `assessmentId` and writes nothing to the assessment. The completion event then reads the object: `observationIds: next.observationIds ?? []` (assurance.ts:2315), so `AssuranceAssessmentCompleted.observationIds` is ALWAYS `[]`, on every completion, however many observations were recorded against it.

THE DRIVEN ARRANGEMENT (node, real engine, one run). Verbatim:
  RecordAssuranceObservation{observationType:'CONFLICT', findingCode:'PRINCIPLE_TESTABILITY', severity:'MATERIAL', statement:'Principle A (testability): the module MUST be split into seams.'} -> ACCEPTED
  RecordAssuranceObservation{observationType:'CONFLICT', findingCode:'PRINCIPLE_COHESION', severity:'MATERIAL', statement:'Principle B (cohesion): the module MUST NOT be split. Directly contradicts Principle A.'} -> ACCEPTED
  obs1 persisted disposition=OPEN ; obs2 persisted disposition=OPEN ; BOTH survive as separate aggregates = true ; assessment.observationIds = []
  CompleteAssuranceAssessment{SATISFIED} while BOTH contradicting principles are OPEN -> ACCEPTED ; assessmentState = SATISFIED ; obs1 disposition AFTER = OPEN ; obs2 disposition AFTER = OPEN
  AssuranceAssessmentCompleted.observationIds = [] ; AssuranceAssessmentCompleted.residualUncertainty = []
CONTROL 1 (the write path is honest, so the gap is the SHAPE not a lost write): re-recording the same observation aggregate with the opposite statement -> CONFLICT | RPH_REVISION_CONFLICT | "Revision conflict on aob_... (actual revision 0)", persisted statement unchanged.
CONTROL 2 (opposing verdicts are not collapsed either): two REQUIRED policies, opposite dispositions on the same subject -> both ACCEPTED, one SATISFIED and one REJECTED standing side by side.

WHY THE NEIGHBOURING DISCLOSURE DOES NOT COVER IT. The completion docblock (assurance.ts:2286-2292) already discloses that `evidenceConsideredIds`, `residualUncertainty` and `recommendedControlActions` read `[]` off the object and are taken from the validatorResult instead - "the object's [] is silence, not a finding of 'none' ... reconciling the object is the §32 increment". `observationIds` is NOT in that list and is the one field still read FROM the object, so the disclosure stops exactly one field short. Likewise `docs/_working/HARMONIZATION-FINDINGS.md:38` (finding 28) names evidenceConsidered / rejectedEvidence / residualUncertainty and not `observationIds`.

SCOPE - THE SECOND CONJUNCT IS BROADER THAN THIS INVARIANT AND THE ENTRY SHOULD SAY SO. An always-empty `observationIds` on the completion event also weakens ASR-4's "durable, inspectable record" and the B7 anti-vacuity rule: any future gate that quantifies over "the assessment's observations" by reading that field would range over nothing and pass. File it system-wide, anchored on ASR-5 limb 8, cross-referenced to ASR-4.

REMEDY. (a) Author a tension carrier - either an optional `relatedObservationIds` / `conflictsWithObservationIds` on `RecordAssuranceObservation` plus its object and event, or a first-class TENSION observationType with a required counterpart id - under the divergence protocol, since the corpus defines no such shape. (b) Append the minted observation id to the assessment's `observationIds` at `recordAssuranceObservation`, so the completion event reports what was actually before the assessor. Red-first for (b): the arrangement above must produce a non-empty `AssuranceAssessmentCompleted.observationIds`, with CONTROL 1 (revision conflict on re-record) still green so the change is proved to be an append and not a rewrite.

CANDIDATE CLUSTER, NOT ASSERTED. limb:ASR-5:6 (no predicate tests a CLAIM SET for joint satisfiability) is the same underlying absence one plane over - the model cannot represent two valid things that conflict - but its remedy is a PREDICATE and this one's is a SHAPE, so they are recorded as separate entries with a cross-reference rather than merged.

evidence:
WHAT THE LIMB FORBIDS: mechanical 'rule violated -> reject' for anything that is not an explicit HARD invariant. Equivalently it requires the engine's reject-on-violation behaviour to be TIERED, with only the hard tier rejecting. It is, and I drove all four rungs.

THE SITE. Gate C of `completeAssuranceAssessment` — `rejectForeclosedDisposition` (assurance.ts:1871), called at assurance.ts:2249, refusing at the cited line. Its predicate: for a POSITIVE disposition, the forbidden set is `BLOCKING_SEVERITIES` ({BLOCKING, CRITICAL}) unioned with whatever the policy's own dispositionRule adds; a completion is refused only if an OPEN observation carries a severity in that set. `BLOCKING_SEVERITIES` is defined in assurance-rules.ts:28 as 'the ladder's own top two rungs', beneath a docblock stating the tiering in terms: 'an open CRITICAL or BLOCKING finding rejects; MATERIAL only conditionally-satisfies'.

DRIVEN ACROSS THE TIER BOUNDARY, WHICH IS THE ONLY WAY TO TELL A LADDER FROM A WALL.
  INFORMATIONAL open -> completion ACCEPTED, assessmentState SATISFIED.
  ADVISORY open      -> completion ACCEPTED, assessmentState SATISFIED.
  BLOCKING open      -> REJECTED, foreclosed.
  CRITICAL open      -> REJECTED, foreclosed.
So a recorded rule violation at the two soft tiers does NOT reject; only the hard tier does. That is the limb, behaving.

AND THE TIERING IS NOT AN AUTHOR'S OPTION IN EITHER DIRECTION. Upward: the floor is UNIONED IN, not defaulted to — the code says 'there is no value an author can write — not `[]`, not omission, not a wrong disposition key — that removes it', so a policy cannot demote a hard invariant out of the rejecting tier. Downward: the union applies to POSITIVE dispositions only, deliberately, so an assessment carrying a blocking finding can still be REJECTED or ESCALATED — the code names that as the case that 'is the control that holds this line'. Both directions matter to this limb: a wall that rejected everything, or one an author could switch off, would each falsify it.

SEPARATELY, the pure kernel implements the same ladder for the disposition itself (`dispositionFromFindings`, assurance-rules.ts:47): open CRITICAL/BLOCKING -> REJECTED; a MATERIAL finding or a partially-met mandatory criterion -> CONDITIONALLY_SATISFIED; only mandatory NOT_MET rejects, where `mandatory` is itself derived from BLOCKING severity (validators.ts:229). Consistent tiering at both layers, from one exported set.

REG-F (new ordinal) — A POLICY MAY DECLARE A SIGNAL-TIER FINDING MECHANICALLY DISPOSITIVE, AND THE ENGINE'S OWN TWIN FIELD PROVES IT KNOWS BETTER.

WHAT CANON REQUIRES. JPWB-DOC-003 §8.2 ASR-5, limb 9 verbatim: "'rule violated → reject' is sufficient only for an explicit hard invariant." The next sentence of the same invariant supplies the reading: "Formalization never upgrades epistemic authority: a compiled smell remains a signal."

WHAT THE CODE DOES. `CreateAssurancePolicy` (packages/rph-application/src/handlers/assurance.ts:173) and `EditAssurancePolicy` (:349) apply NO range check to `dispositionRules[].forbiddenOpenSeverities`. The field is `z.array(z.string()).optional()` on `DispositionRuleSchema` (packages/rph-contracts/src/objects.ts:214) — a bare string array. Gate C, `rejectForeclosedDisposition` (assurance.ts:1867-1911), then honours whatever the author wrote: at :1901 `const forbidden = new Set([...floor, ...(dispositionRule?.forbiddenOpenSeverities ?? [])]);` and at :1908 it refuses. So an open INFORMATIONAL or ADVISORY observation can mechanically foreclose a SATISFIED disposition — 'rule violated → reject' at canon's own paradigm tier for a signal.

THE DISCRIMINATOR IS TWENTY LINES AWAY IN THE SAME FILE. The twin severity-shortcut array IS range-checked. `rejectUnratifiedEscalationSeverities` (assurance.ts:116-140) rejects any `escalationRules[].escalateOnOpenSeverities` value outside `ESCALATABLE_SEVERITIES = new Set(['CRITICAL'])` (assurance.ts:97), and it is called on BOTH authoring paths, at :176 and :367. Its docblock (assurance.ts:113-115) gives the reason in this limb's own terms: "fail closed at authoring rather than persist a silently-inert rule … and direct any deliberate override to the ratified `EscalationRule.trigger` (§13)." Two arrays of severity strings, one command, twenty lines apart; one hard-checked, the other unchecked.

THE DRIVEN ARRANGEMENT (scratchpad/v4_asr5_9.mjs and v4_asr5_9b.mjs, node, controls in the same run). CONTROL, the twin field: `CreateAssurancePolicy{escalationRules:[{trigger:{},escalationTarget:'ARCHITECT',requiredPackage:[],escalateOnOpenSeverities:['INFORMATIONAL']}]}` -> REJECTED | RPH_VALIDATION_SEMANTIC_FAILED | "escalationRules.escalateOnOpenSeverities accepts only CRITICAL — the single severity §10.3's default precedence pairs with ESCALATED; got [INFORMATIONAL]…"; the same policy with ['CRITICAL'] -> ACCEPTED, so the guard discriminates. THE ARRANGEMENT: `CreateAssurancePolicy{dispositionRules:[{disposition:'SATISFIED',condition:{},forbiddenOpenSeverities:['INFORMATIONAL']}]}` -> ACCEPTED; then `RecordAssuranceObservation{observationType:'RECOMMENDATION',severity:'INFORMATIONAL',statement:'A heuristic: consider splitting.'}` -> ACCEPTED (persisted OPEN); then `CompleteAssuranceAssessment{dispositionRecommendation:'SATISFIED'}` -> REJECTED | RPH_VALIDATION_SEMANTIC_FAILED | "CompleteAssuranceAssessment: a SATISFIED disposition is foreclosed — the policy's dispositionRules forbid it while an observation of severity [INFORMATIONAL] is still OPEN (DOC-004 §10.3). Resolve or waive the finding, or return a non-satisfied disposition."; assessmentState = ASSESSING. BYTE-ADJACENT CONTROL, the authored rule removed, same INFORMATIONAL observation: `CompleteAssuranceAssessment{SATISFIED}` -> ACCEPTED, assessmentState = SATISFIED. NOT AN 'INFORMATIONAL' QUIRK: ['ADVISORY'] with an ADVISORY RECOMMENDATION open -> REJECTED, identical message at [ADVISORY]. NO RANGE CHECK OF ANY KIND: ['NOT_A_SEVERITY_AT_ALL'] -> ACCEPTED at authoring and then silently inert — precisely the failure mode the twin guard's docblock says it exists to prevent. BOTH AUTHORING PATHS: EditAssurancePolicy adding escalateOnOpenSeverities:['INFORMATIONAL'] -> REJECTED; EditAssurancePolicy adding forbiddenOpenSeverities:['INFORMATIONAL'] -> ACCEPTED.

THE GOVERNING PRIOR DECISION, RECORDED RATHER THAN RE-LITIGATED. REG-D-042 (docs/canon/JPWB-REG-005:3249) and docs/_working/DESIGN-tier-tailoring-is-a-ratchet.md §3.1 ruled that the floor is UNIONED IN and that "a policy may only ADD severities it will not tolerate" — the handler comment at assurance.ts:1893 states it in those words — and that ruling is CORRECT AND MUST STAND. But its entire subject is the SUBTRACT direction: that an author's silence, an empty array, or a wrong disposition key must not switch the de minimis floor off. It never asks whether a severity BELOW the hard tier may be ADDED. This entry answers that unasked half, and answers it the way the same repository already answered it for the escalation twin.

THE REMEDY, deliberately NOT a schema change. `forbiddenOpenSeverities`' bare `string[]` typing is a RECORDED deliberate choice (docs/_working/HARMONIZATION-LOG.md:3226 — "kept verbatim string[], not a closed AssuranceSeverity[] — the doc's own asymmetry, preserved, not 'improved.'"). The remedy is a handler-level authoring guard mirroring assurance.ts:116 at both call sites (:176 and :367): a severity a policy ADDS to `forbiddenOpenSeverities` must lie in the hard tier (`BLOCKING_SEVERITIES`, packages/rph-assurance/src/assurance-rules.ts:28), anything below it refused and directed to the ratified `DispositionRule.condition`, exactly as the escalation guard directs to `EscalationRule.trigger`; a value outside `AssuranceSeverity` altogether refused for the twin's own stated reason — do not persist a silently-inert rule.

WHAT THE LIMB FORBIDS: letting an execution trace stand as support for the proposition that the OUTCOME SATISFIES INTENT, when all it shows is that execution occurred. WHAT THE CODE DOES: nothing anywhere relates an Evidence object's evidenceType to the proposition it is offered for. I drove the conflation on TWO planes and it was accepted on both.

PLANE 1 — CLAIM SUPPORT. ProposeEvidence(evidenceType:'TRACE', scope:'execution trace of step S1: the step ran to completion') -> ACCEPTED; AdmitEvidence(admittedScope: the same string) -> ACCEPTED, evidence.status=ADMISSIBLE; then RecordClaimAssessment(SUPPORTED) against a FITNESS claim whose statement is literally 'The delivered outcome satisfies the approved Product Intent.' -> ACCEPTED, claim.status=SUPPORTED with supportingEvidenceIds naming the trace. The engine now records, authoritatively, that an intent-satisfaction claim is SUPPORTED and that its support is an execution trace.

PLANE 2 — EVIDENCE REQUIREMENTS. A policy declaring requiredEvidence [{id:'EV-1', evidenceType:'TEST_RESULT', cardinality:'AT_LEAST_ONE', requiredForDispositions:'SATISFIED_ONLY'}]; I proposed and admitted an Evidence object whose actual evidenceType is TRACE and submitted it as satisfying EV-1 with the payload's free-string evidenceType:'TEST_RESULT'. ACCEPTED. store.loadObject(E2).state.evidenceType still reads TRACE. CompleteAssuranceAssessment(SATISFIED) then ACCEPTED and the assessment reached SATISFIED — the TEST_RESULT requirement discharged by a trace. SubmitEvidenceForAssessmentPayloadSchema types evidenceType as z.string().optional() and the handler (packages/rph-application/src/handlers/assurance.ts:1480-1600) never loads the Evidence object to compare it.

WHY THE ARM. The refusal machinery on both commands is alive and discriminating (see sibling_control), so this is admission, not absence of a site. `evidenceType` is written and copied and never once compared (census).

NOT DOUBLE-COUNTED WITH ASR-6:6. ASR-6's last sentence ('Evidence cannot support a claim outside its declared scope without an explicit assessment') owns the general scope-vs-claim comparison and RPH-EVD-004 files that gap for passing tests. THIS limb is a TYPE/PROPOSITION conflation, not a scope-breadth one: the trace's scope was stated fully and accurately ('the step ran to completion') and it still supported 'the outcome satisfies intent'. Nothing in the register or the ledger names a trace, an execution artifact, or the execution-occurred/intent-satisfied distinction on the EVIDENCE plane.

WHAT THE LIMB FORBIDS: deriving test ADEQUACY from a COUNT. THE ENGINE'S ONLY ADEQUACY COMPUTATION IS EXACTLY THAT COUNT, and I drove it.

THE MECHANISM. packages/rph-application/src/handlers/assurance.ts:1186-1187 defines `demandsAnInstance = (r) => r?.cardinality !== 'ZERO_OR_MORE'`. Every 'is this evidence requirement met?' decision in the engine — the EVIDENCE_PENDING -> READY arrow in `submitEvidenceForAssessment`, and Gate A in `completeAssuranceAssessment` (assurance.ts:1986-1996) — is `required MINUS received`, i.e. does a receipt EXIST. So a policy requirement declaring evidenceType TEST_RESULT and cardinality AT_LEAST_ONE is discharged by exactly one receipt, whatever that one artifact contains, and the assessment is then free to be SATISFIED. Driven: one TEST_RESULT whose own scope string is 'one unit test of one function' took the assessment to READY, and CompleteAssuranceAssessment(SATISFIED) was ACCEPTED.

The only thing refused is a byte-duplicate receipt of the SAME pair. Adequacy therefore reduces to a threshold of one, and nothing about the tests' oracle, breadth or risk-proportionality is consulted.

WHAT CANON REQUIRES. JPWB-DOC-003 §7 ASR-9, limb 7 (canon L277), verbatim: "The condition remains visible in the assessment, the PWU assurance view, review packages, and baseline packages, and persists after parent baselining;". FOUR surfaces plus a persistence clause. Surface 2 is carried; surface 1 is already disclosed at two code sites; the filing is about the other three, and it has FOUR components that must not be merged.

(1) THE §38 `controlActions` FIELD IS DEAD BY CONSTRUCTION, INSIDE THE SURFACE THE REGISTER CREDITS AS WORKING — AND THE TEST THAT SHOULD HAVE CAUGHT IT IS GREEN ON AN INADMISSIBLE FIXTURE. packages/rph-projections/src/assurance-view.ts:263 reads `controlActions: strArr(p.recommendedControlActions)`; `strArr` (assurance-view.ts:134-135) keeps only `typeof x === 'string'`. The contract types that field as OBJECTS: `recommendedControlActions: z.array(ControlActionRecommendationSchema)` (messages.ts:859, objects.ts:571) with `ControlActionRecommendationSchema = z.record(z.string(), z.unknown())` (objects.ts:82). DRIVEN, BOTH ARMS: the object form is ACCEPTED and the view row reads `controlActions = []`; the bare-string form — the only shape `strArr` would keep — is refused VALIDATION_FAILED | RPH_VALIDATION_SCHEMA_FAILED at the boundary. There is no admissible input for which that field is ever non-empty: a measured impossibility, not an unreachable-input hypothesis. CONTROLS: `openConditions`, folded by the SAME function from the SAME event, reads ["offline sync deferred to a successor PWU"]; an unconditional (SATISFIED) completion drops it to [] — the fold is alive and the disposition gate is real.
⚠ AND THE INSTRUMENT EXISTS, WAS AIMED AT THIS FIELD, AND IS GREEN ON AN EVENT THE ENGINE CANNOT EMIT. packages/rph-projections/src/assurance-view.test.ts:336 asserts `expect(a.controlActions).toEqual(['GATHER_EVIDENCE','REQUEST_HUMAN_DECISION'])`. It passes on a hand-built fixture at :329 whose `recommendedControlActions` is an array of BARE STRINGS, fed through an `evt()` helper (:22) that types `payload: unknown` and validates nothing. The fixture fails `AssuranceAssessmentCompletedPayloadSchema.safeParse` with {"expected":"record","code":"invalid_type","path":["recommendedControlActions",0]}, while the object form parses true. This is the core of the filing, because RPH-ASR-009's own disposition says "if the projections DID drop the condition, the instrument that would catch it is a projection test, not this register" — the register is right about WHERE the instrument lives and wrong that it is working.
⚠ AND TWO CORPORA ASSERT THE OPPOSITE, which is why a reader stops: assurance-view.ts:36-40 lists `controlActions` under POPULATED and carries its own CORRECTION note ("an earlier note here filed this UNSOURCED … the datum was on the wire all along", and it even calls the field "the 23-value ControlAction enum", which it is not), and docs/_working/HARMONIZATION-LOG.md:3441-3447 records Increment F moving it "to POPULATED". A false-POSITIVE claim.

(2) SURFACES 3 AND 4 DO NOT EXIST, AND THE REGISTER'S DISPOSITION PRESUMES THEY DO. Censuses re-run this pass with an observed positive control over the identical population and filters: `REVIEW_PACKAGE|ReviewPackage|reviewPackage` -> 0 and `BASELINE_PACKAGE|BaselinePackage|baselinePackage` -> 0 across packages/ + apps/ excluding /dist/ and .svelte-kit, against `ASSURANCE_ASSESSMENT` -> 68 FILES. Content direction, not identifiers: `review package|baseline package` -> 4 hits and NOT ONE is an implementation. RPH-ASR-009 (packages/rph-domain/src/enforcement-register.ts:1307-1326) dispositions the rule NOT_A_COMMAND_REFUSAL with the note "JPWB-DOC-003 §7 carries all four surfaces verbatim — and all four are projections, which is the disposition", and its `why` (:1317) enumerates "the assessment object, the PWU assurance view, the review package and the baseline package". Two of those four have zero implementation while the corpus ratifies them in detail (JPWB-DOC-001 §7.2; docs/canon/_extracts/extract-doc006.md:50, eight required components including residual uncertainty; extract-doc008-b.md:36). Ratified and unbuilt is the opposite of "canon says nothing".
⚠ PARTIALLY RECORDED ALREADY — CITE, DO NOT RE-FILE, THE REVIEW-PACKAGE HALF. docs/_working/AUDIT-shape-survivorship-2026-08-20.md:144 carries the row "| HumanReviewPackage (§37) | ABSENT | Search claim, both directions: (1) name — repo-wide grep for 'HumanReviewPackage' … hits ONLY RPH-DOC-004 itself; (2) content — grep for decisionRequested¦executiveSummary¦materialClaims¦availableOptions…", and :370 records the independent refutation stage: "HELD. It does NOT record the BASELINE-package half, and it does not record that RPH-ASR-009's disposition rests on both surfaces existing — which is what this component adds.

evidence: NOTHING IN THIS ENGINE MARKS ANYTHING AS DEFERRED, SO NOTHING CAN CHECK THAT A DEFERRAL STAYS REPRESENTED. The word does not appear in the contracts at all: `grep -c -i defer` over packages/rph-contracts/src/objects.ts, messages.ts and enums.ts returns 0, 0, 0, while the same three files return 2, 3, 0 for 'residual' — so the population is alive and the zeros are real. There is no DeferScope command, no `deferred` field, no DeferralRecorded event. I WENT THROUGH CANON'S FIVE NAMED CARRIERS ONE AT A TIME rather than treating them as a phrase: (1) ASSUMPTION — exists, mintable (`DetectAssumption` / `DiscloseAssumption` in the 105-command registry, ASSUMPTION object with a status machine); (2) CONSTRAINT — exists, mintable (`AssertConstraint`, packages/rph-application/src/handlers/obligation-constraint.ts, ConstraintObject with `strength` MANDATORY|PREFERRED|ADVISORY); (3) RESIDUAL CONDITION — exists on the completion EVENT only and is dropped from the assessment object (limb 7's finding); (4) BASELINE SCOPE STATEMENT — the field exists and is a FABRICATED CONSTANT: `BaselineObjectSchema` requires `scope: z.string()` (objects.ts:694) but `CreateBaselinePayloadSchema` (messages.ts:375-379) has only baselineType, itemObjectIds and optional assuranceAssessmentIds, so packages/rph-application/src/handlers/governance.ts:747 hardcodes `scope: 'undertaking'` for every baseline ever created — I read it back off a driven baseline and it is literally "undertaking"; (5) FUTURE OBLIGATION — exists, mintable (`AssertObligation`, strength MANDATORY|CONDITIONAL|ADVISORY). So four of five carriers are real objects and one is a constant — and NOT ONE OF THEM IS EVER WRITTEN BECAUSE SOMETHING WAS DEFERRED. There is no producer and therefore no conservation question. THE 'NEVER SILENTLY DELETED' HALF IS VACUOUSLY TRUE, AND VACUITY IS NOT ENFORCEMENT: a PWU's scope statement is immutable by construction — `boundaries` is written at exactly one site, `proposePwu` (packages/rph-application/src/handlers/pwu.ts:323), read at pwu.ts:733-743 by the §9.1 readiness guard, and edited by NO command (`ReshapePwu` is a lifecycle arrow to RESHAPING, pwu.ts:857-871, and carries only `reason` and `triggeringObjectId`; `boundaries` appears exactly once in messages.ts, at line 125, on the ProposePwu payload). So `outOfScope` cannot be silently deleted because it cannot be changed at all. That makes deletion INEXPRESSIBLE, but it does not make the limb enforced, because the limb's operative content is that a deferral IS REPRESENTED — and nothing puts one there to preserve.

The filing should say three things. (1) THE CONCEPT IS ABSENT, NOT THE CHECK: filing this as 'a missing guard' would misdirect the remedy, because a guard needs a producer and there is none — the shape owed is a way to RECORD a deferral, and only then a check that it is carried. (2) `outOfScope` IS THE HAZARD, NOT THE ANSWER: it is the only scope-shaped field, it is immutable after ProposePwu, and it cannot distinguish 'never in scope' from 'in scope, deferred' — so a future increment that reads deferral out of `outOfScope` would be inferring professional meaning from a field that does not carry it, which CON-000 AX-6 forbids by name. (3) THE 'BASELINE SCOPE STATEMENT' CARRIER IS INERT and should be fixed as part of any deferral work: `CreateBaseline` cannot supply `scope`, so governance.ts:747 writes the literal 'undertaking' on every baseline; the same defect is owed under limb 7 for a different reason (the baseline as a visibility surface), and the two should be closed together rather than twice. ⚠ AND A NOTE AGAINST THE LIMB SPLIT (rule w3b-limb-split/1.0.0), raised rather than acted on: limb 10 bundles a five-way disjunction of carriers with a prohibition ('never silently deleted'), and those two score differently — the carriers are four-fifths present and the prohibition is vacuously satisfied by immutability.
